I want to love this game with all my heart but i cant. Dont get me wrong this game is extremely enjoyable, The concept is great and addictive. Everything is perfect and fun untill it becomes more than its worth in terms of effort. At some point it bcomes apparent that the concept is muddied by the fact that you control every tiny aspect of the crew and their actions, which isnt a bad thing, but becomes harder than you think at first.
Here are some of the largest cons
Gunners:
The gunners will not fire at anything unless you spot it for them. This wouldnt be an issue if at some point later on they had some kind of skill that allowed them to at least respond to incoming fire solo. Instead they sit there and drool untill they die or you manage to spot a target for them.
The gunners do not learn any form of accuracy as they gain experience, Even the focus fire skill lead them to just hosing a specific area a fighter resides, only now they dont let off the trigger untill they run out of ammo of the skill runs out. this leads to later aces who maneuvers are sporadic patterns and passes being impossible to defend against.
Piloting:
The pilot will not move so much as an inch without you spotting a nav point or issueing the single evasion command. This means that the second an enemy BF110 gets under you, theres about 3 seconds to hit the corckscrew command before you lose every gunner in the tail. This command may or may not spike you into the ground and upon completion , this also leaves you manauverless for quite some time.  The slight ability to sway from side to side to mildly evade fire from below automatically or even adding just one more skill to aid with moving the largest target in the sky would help a lot.
Navigation:
No matter your level you wlll find you cannot go above low altitude, You're Navigator couldnt see the ground if he stood atop a ladder. There is no dynamic weather system allowing the option to use height on a clear day, Its just permanently cowdy. At high Altitude you can navigate by the stars but you wont get the chance before your crew freezes to death. Even with the addition of adequate therman clothing the lack of any ability for the navigator to see the ground or select a time of flight so they can nav by the stars leaves many grand slam missions a bust. You must drop from high altitude but the second you get close all markers cease, the navigator has recinded his directions and essentially becomes a usless member untill you drop to a low altitude at which the bomb is ineffective adn you fail the mission.
Missions:
Missions get repetative, moreso when you constantly lose bombers and crews and are more or less forced to grind the same route repeatedly untill you can get enough upgrades to attempt a campaign mission
The grind:
Heres where its interesting, its really a core concept to how the game itself is meant to be.Historically bomber losses were frequent, The constant need to build and recruit often to replace lost crews and planes is reflected in this game.
As long as you complete an objective you get the mney and research. You wont always make it home but you can try and refit the next bomber. The biggest issue is this gets increasngly frustrating and difficult as the campaign goes on. For instance i had a crew that somehow made it back for 28 missions and only lost two members. Im close to the end of the capaigns and i lost everything, All crew aboard were killed before the pilot went and the bomber fell out of the sky, now im back to square one.
This all makes sense and is one of the concepts i like in the game. I get fresh recruits. but they have the same skills as the early war men, No training improvements to ready them for the changes that you face currently. You're bomber is back to square one aswell. No factory fresh improvments for the year. This turns the learning curve into a cliff, pure luck might get this new un upgraded bomber back to base with at least 4 men alive. At this point the game stops,There is no real way to continue without constantly starting back over with the same stuff. There is no way around restarting, towards the end game, no matter how good your crew or aircraft has become. No matter your experienced crew or upgrades to the bomber every trip becomes one way. There is no return trip anymore and the fight turns iinto equipping the bomber to survive the 3-4 minutes till you can drop bombs
Personally i think the option for a new front, different bomber choices, ,more missions would make this cliff more palateble regardless of game progress. Rinse repeat is a tired trope and this is very barebones rinse repeat.
overall its an amazing concept, one in a million actually enjoyable game. but for the price i stales quicker than im willing to recomend.

You can certainly understand people who may take one look at this game, see how wonky it looks, and run a mile.
It certainly took me several attempts to get into this game, but by the time I had the combat down pat, and had gotten used to the somewhat shaky, old engine, I really came to enjoy The Witcher immensely.
The combat is different, of course, but is a a far cry from button mashing, and once you have the timing sorted, it will become second nature. The higher difficulties also ensure that you use the FULL advantages of the alchemy system, and levelling up different traits and signs in a certain manner give an RPG experience that belies the impression the opening segment's wonkiness can give off.
The story engrossed me, and I had to really agonise over some of the choices the first time round (at time of writing, I have yet to try the alternatives) and the game showed that every choice has consequences - they are neither "right" or "wrong", but they have an effect on the story either way.
The voice acting, sadly, is a little narmy, but strangely fits right in with the wonkiness. A few NPC quips in Vizima had me rolling around laughing the first time I heard them, partly because of the voice acting, but also partly for the gratiuitousness of the dialogue. It does, however, sometimes detract from some of the more serious moments albeit not taking you right out.
(Incidentally, I gave this a write-in vote for the 2017 Steam Autumn Sale awards for the "Most gratuitousness use of the word "Belgium" in a serious game" - I bet Thaler doesn't own a swear box.)
The side quests give you a great deal to do as well, and work very well alongside the main quest. Just remember to save before playing a game of poker dice though - the CPU is a cheating sod!
Overall: sure, it doesn't look great next to it's sequels, but this game is still a fantastic opening entry in the trilogy. Honestly, do your best to stick with the faults and you may enjoy this game as much as I did. CDPR did great work on what I believe is their first release and laid the groundwork for the greatness that followed.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I've played for two hours and was actually able to complete the game in this time. Initially I was uncertain whether it was a good choice considering that it's got $20 price tag, however;
- It was overall really really fun, it's buggy but some of the bugs made the game even more entertaining
- BUT the full game isn't actually available yet, you will reach a sign saying after only an hour or two that says 'end of early access, check for updates’ and a dead end
Okay to start off with you are are in a world with a theme that borrows heavily from Quake II. I loved that game. You get to play as a Strogg. They don't actually call themselves Strogg but I'm just going to refer to them as Strogg. I was very happy to get to be a Strogg =). I decapitated my superior officer with my salute and off I went. Initially combat wasn't so great. You have a blaster but it's nowhere near as cool as the real Quake II blaster. I found it hard to aim, you need to be very precise and I found it hard to fine tune aiming with the mouse in this game. However after playing for sometime I found aiming easier, so I may have just needed time to adjust. I still think your projectiles need to be bigger, especially your rockets. By the way the rocket launcher in this game has an identity crisis, it doesn’t know whether its a rocket launch or a rail gun lol. I soon found myself in a section playing domination i.e. capture all the points against the AI. That part is a bit of a work in progress, I think they could flesh it out quite a bit more. After taking the points I fought a boss in the next area. It was a cool Quake II style cyborg tank.
_____However I had trouble progressing through this section. At first it just killed me because it was too strong. Then I was unable to confront it again several times because the guard you need to kill to trigger the boss fight just wouldn't die no matter how many limbs I chopped off of him. So I had to reload and start from the end of the last area a few times until it worked. It also took me a while to discover the chaingun you need to defeat the boss.
_____Combat started to get more fun at this stage, mainly because there were more enemies. Sometimes you have specific objectives but they can be a little buggy or apparently not fully implemented e.g. at one point I was supposed to proceed to a tower and destroy it. However as soon as I made my way to the tower I was given the next objective without having destroying a thing. Gameplay mainly consists of heading to the next area and fighting through the enemies.
_____Along the way were some sort of alternate dimension instances filled with purple metallic platforms as well. There wasn't much to these areas but they were interesting locations, sort of like a non-organic version of the alternate dimension in the Half-Life series.
_____There is one bug at the moment which persistently made the game difficult and apparently it is something to do with the gravity levels. I found that when I reloaded after dying the gravity is for some reason extremely high. You are unable to jump, jump pads a rendered useless and for some reason it creates a really big frame rate drop. Until this bug is fixed in a patch the only way I could find to return the game to normal is by restarting it. This doesn't take long to do, just use quicksave so that you don't lose any progress. There is a bright side to this issue, it causes enemies to do cart-wheels when they die =)
After completing the Strogg act you find yourself in a World War II themed area fighting Germans on your way to church. Unfortunately the game ends before you get to your destination. I never actually saw some of the locations and weapons featured in the screenshots on the steam page.
The game doesn't look too bad. Obviously it is intended to look like older titles. Make sure you choose the right aspect screen ratio in the display menu. For some reason mine was incorrect by default and I spent the first half hour or so unable to see most of my HUD. Also the game looked a lot better after tweaking this.
_____Did I mention that I really liked being a Strogg? =) You retain this form throughout the game even during the WW2 section, which was cool.
_____I found several visually entertaining bugs or unintended features. You can pick up dropped enemy weapons with E and launch them out of the map with left click. You can pick up corpses and flail them about around like Ragdolls. Sometimes amputated limbs of enemies will roll continuously without stopping. I sliced of a Strogg's head and it rolled all the way across a large room bounced off the wall and kept on rolling. Usually the AI is good at aggressively finding you and hunting you down but sometimes enemies spin around continuously or walk around and around in tight circles. If you shoot enemies with the crossbow it takes them to the ground in a low arc and pins them there instead of carrying them at high speed to the surface behind them. Some of the stuff I saw I think should be left as it is =)
_____The dialogue wasn't always amazing sometimes it was amusing. I found it a bit painful to hear feigned American accents however, especially when I had to repeat that scene multiple times. Some of the sound effects sound like they are straight out of familiar old titles, which was pretty good for nostalgic reasons.
So yeah I did enjoy enjoy playing this. But I do think $20 is a bit much for what you are getting at least at the moment. I was expecting a full albeit buggy game. Yes I would have preferred not to have been set back so much to buy this game. But I'm not too worried about it personally. However I'm pretty sure it's guaranteed that a lot of people would not be happy to pay $20 for what they would get get in this case.

First up, I am writing this review as how it plays today.  It's annoying reading someone's review and it starts out something like this:  "I remember when this first came out and blah blah blah"  and they're reminiscing of the good old days and basing their review on the experience they had when it was new.  I mean, the original Wolfenstein and Doom was awesome back in its time but to rate it on todays standards they're pretty crappy..
Although this game is dated in its appearance, it is stll loads of fun!  You can literally sit on it for hours it's one of those games you lose track of time with as you start to hear birds outside for the sun is coming up.. I have this game on GoG but got it in a package here on Steam, and after reading in other people's reviews they said its buggy and keeps crashing, I thought I'd test it out to see if it runs OK.. Well, 4 hours whooshed by as I got stuck into a new game of it as a blacksmith, worked my way up to goldsmith and now I'm looking for a wife coz if you dont have any kids there's no one to carry on your business and estates!
As for bugs and/or crashed?  Zero.. Game runs fine on Windows 7 with a nvidia graphics card.  The graphics are quite dated as to be expected it's over 10 years old.  Perhaps other users didn't run the graphics first time set up correctly?  It does ask for your primary graphics, and an option when you click play "Launch with newer graphics card"...  Well everyone's rig is different so who knows what is conflicting with them, but as for me I didn't have any problems but I'm sure there are ways to fix it if you do experience any faults.
The learning curve seems a bit steep at first.  If you jump into a new game with no knowledge how the mechanics work I doubt you will get far.  There are tutorials to go thru accessed in the main menu, enough to get you started and once you pick it up you can lose yourself in the game.  And there always seems to be new stuff to discover.  For example, you can run for government positions and the higher up you go, there are more perks such as additional income, and abilities to change tax rates, laws, etc..
So when you start a new game, you choose what profession you wish to be.  Blacksmith, Carpenter, Perfumer, Priest, Gravedigger, just to name some.  Each profession has different things to be done, and has different benefits that can help you.  And example here would be a carpenter can make a toy, and usually you would sell them at the marketplace but if you have kids, you want them to be happy and do well so you can give them as a gift.  You can still do that as a blacksmith but you would just have to buy the toy at the sell price from the marketplace.  A goldsmith can make jewellery to woo a potential wife, and so on.  There is so much to do in this game, while you're expanding your business, hiring more employees, improving your workshops, buying raw materials, selling finished products, extending your home, learning new skills, blackmailing an official, bribing a judge, finding a wife (especially good if she is rich, boost the ol' bank ballance!), having some kids, putting them though school, making sure they get into the best university so when you kick the bucket they have the best stats you can give them and then you carry on the game as them!
Starting a new game as a different profession is almost an entire new game in itself.  Choosing a city to start in determines the difficutly, building areas, size, etc.. I haven't even tried them all yet, some are more difficult and require a whole different approach.  Some differ as in the trade you choose, the products and materials needed are different, as a thief you are pickpocketing and scouting homes and businesses, robbing trade carts, etc.  As a grave digger you're digging up bones and making stuff with it, as a priest you're in a church making paper and writing scrolls..
It really is pretty addicitive, and not quite like any other game.  It's very complex but only as much as you want it to be.  You can go thru an entire game just growing your business buy making and selling stuff... Or you apsire to be emperor, climbing your way up the political ladder, gathering dirt on your opponents, starting rumors, sabotaging, and all sorts of stuff... And if you pick it up on special for $1.99 like it is now, it's well worth it.. And if you're too late and it's back to its normal price of $9.99 then pop it on your wishlist and wait for the xmas sales ;)

You can definitely beat it without using a walkthrough, just be sure to use your brain and explore the world.

I gave this a try because I like to keep abreast of the MMO world by trying as many titles as possible. I mention this because I had very low expectations of DCUO going in, but to my surprise, it's actually pretty good.
The combat has a good sense of weight to it, and they really get the "you have super powers" feeling down. Fence in your way? Punch it down. Jumped by a bunch of enemies? Throw a dumpster at them. The movement powers are similarily thrilling, allowing you to run, fly, and leap with fantastic speed and agility.
There are a few issues -- occasional pop-ups advertising the cash shop, lack of variation in content between playing a hero or a villain, and somewhat generic questing -- but on the whole, DC Universe Online is a very solid game, and I came away mystified as to why it isn't more popular.
Unfortunately, I could not be less interested in DC or its lore, so I didn't stick around long, but if you enjoy DC or care more about game mechanics than story or setting, I'd definitely give this game a go. Even with my dislike for DC, I'm still tempted to give it another go sometimes.

When DC announced the marriage of DC Universe Online, I think every single nerd on the planet immediately said to themselves, "This can go one of two ways; pretty damned awesome or the most excruciating experience invented since the bikini wax."  And lo and behold, we met the second most painful item to hit mankind.  Originally, the developing company hyped up the game, promising everything from customizable player housing, villian and hero PvP that would be well-balanced and enjoyable, as well as a relentless assault on the typical flavor of the week scenarios and power upgrades.  They promised scenarios and power types that have actually existed in the DC comic genre.  Out of all of their promises, they've fulfilled two.  In a ratio based item, that's 2:45.
In general, that's bad business.  When they discovered that they were unable to or were expected to keep their promises, they quickly went the route of the current MMO genre; free to play.  Since then, the game has constantly had ill-repairs, downtime, unmet promises, and very, very low expectations.  It is just one step above Champions Online, save for the strange Mortal Combat type figurations for certain attack moves (down, down-right, right anyone?).  DC Universe actually has a storyline, which is impressive given its current state of affairs in-game.  Character customization is lacking.  The developing company (mainly their PR branch) continues to promise amazing new feats, outfits, and customization that will resurrect its game in a manner that would put an unnamed fellow from 2000 some years ago to shame.  Unfortunately, thus far, they've only been able to resurrect a continual decline in player data-base, as well as overall effectiveness.
However, they still offer a plate of cookies and a strangely colored kool-aid.

Operation Raccoon City takes us back to where it all started and treads a path laiden with familiar setpieces that fans of the franchise have known and loved. However its an almost straight console port with an antiquated GFWL messing with the program (nothing a google search for a fix cannot solve) but it did have trouble appealing to diehard fans of the Resident Evil franchise and thusly is an experience largely overlooked, by no means is this a 'bad' game but it had every opportunity to be so much greater than what it is.
Operation Raccoon City's greatest strength is also its greatest weakness, a non-canonical and self contained story set between the events of much beloved Resident Evil 2 and 3 sees a USS Operative team initially led by HUNK; are taken through the events that transpired to bring Raccoon City to its knees. Initially the story remains on-canon with the rest of the timeline until your team is tasked with wiping out central characters of the Resident Evil franchise, namely Leon Scott Kennedy, Claire Redfield, Jill Valentine and anyone else who happens to wander into your path, this is where the game begins to flounder like a fish trapped in a wine glass. That isn't to say the story is terrible, but it muddies itself with getting involved in 'what-if' scenarios rather than choosing to focus on Umbrella's more devious wetwork conspiracies and opting 'out' to remain behind the shadows. It is because of this the story fails to be anything memorable or meaningful by distancing itself as far away from the canon of Resident Evil as it can which in the end is a great shame for something that had so much potential. Digressing away for a moment however, the very standalone nature of the narrative and its daring to turn away from the fans expectations to offer a new perspective is refreshing and should be commended; after all, there are no cliffhangers or questions left unanswered come the finale and the wake of all your destrution, so it does earn its merits there.
Gameplay wise, its a mixed bag of nuts. A four player co-op campaign is there and with friends, its a great experience, a choice of 8 playable characters all with their own individual perks and playstyles can be upgraded through a below average levelling system in which you spend your hard earned XP for weapons, passive or combat skills. The controls are designed for gamepads in mind, the mouse and keyboard setup doesn't really work too well and navigating the environment rests between clunky or fluid. You wouldn't press a button and accidentally do something else but the accurate responses just dont quite hit the mark they should. Your adversaries are lethal bullet sponges and often will take more than a full clip of ammunition to bring them down. With online co-op, coordinated attacks can mean the difference between life and death and this can actually be joyous fun.
As a single player experience it has the potential to be quite frustrating as your teams AI is lacking in some departments, yet excels in others. For example, they can manage themselves when it comes to healing, shooting or finding the nearest shady spot in an all out firefight but in close range combat they have a hard time deciding whether to go melee or gunsa'blazing, often resulting in their death through lack of final decision.
The difficulty during missions can spike at key chokeholds found throughout the game, you could be sailing through one moment and suddenly you're watching the load screen time after time wondering what the hell happened? Even on a moderate difficulty setting the game will contest you for dominance, which for some, might be no bad thing; yet for others it will just be an aggrivating nightmare.
Ammunition is always in abundance so the survival horror aspect is largely withdrawn in favour of running and gunning but if you ARE on a higher difficulty setting then you'll see its just as well with my points mentioned above. There is also, in all difficulties a pretty cool feature which can have the player contract the zombifying virus if they absorb too much damage or become infected when heavily bleeding, which puts on a desperate scramble for an anti-viral container to cure yourself before you turn and start eating your friends, all of which are limited in number throughout each chapter of the game. Death is not permenent when playing online with friends but offline, the AI are incapable of reviving you so being downed is a no-no unless you dont mind a fair bit of backtracking from the last checkpoint.
There is some exploration to be had albiet completely optional, searching for CCTV cameras, token recording devices or laptops that reward you with additional XP and concept art unlocks in the gallery menu. All obtainable while looting for keys or switches to doors that were previously locked. So although levels seem linear, there is some exploration to be had, even if it is only minor deviations from your current tasks.
In conclusion the game is not terrible by any means but it is a misfire on something so full of potential. Its like a cheap mulled wine, merlot or chardonnay; take your pick. Its a cheap, pleasant experience that gets the job done but you'll find yourself with a dry taste in your mouth at the end and if you drank too much of it, probably a bit of a headache. Still, an experience worth visiting if you can pick it up on sale with a few friends who are daring enough to give something new, yet old a try.

Great game, annoying as all hell fanbase. I first came into the Elder Scrolls series with Oblivion and was absolutely absorbed into Skyrim once the game finally released. Now considering myself a die-hard fan of the Elder Scrolls, I took to the internet and found that many considered Oblivion and Skyrim to both be dumbed-down knockoffs of the series' true crowning achievement: Morrowind. I was intrigued by the idea that what had become my favorite game series was spawned from what was apparently a flawless masterpiece that I had yet to experience, so I picked the game up on Steam immediately. I was then treated to appalling graphics with a draw distance shorter than I can throw a football (which isn't far), characters who walked around like they'd just completed a cycling tour of Europe, and fetch quests galore (Gathering mushrooms for the Mages Guild, anyone?). I then forgot about the game for several months until the ESO update announcement put it back into my consciousness. I decided that I owed it to myself to figure out what it was that made people adore this game so much and started a new playthrough. This time, I felt that I was finally seeing the game's charm. Quests without objective markers meant that some modicum of mental effort was actually required to complete them, giving a real sense of weight and accomplishment to even the most simple of tasks. The story and lore were rich and layered, not shying away from unsavory topics like slavery, drug abuse, and religious persecution. The combat, while lacking the fun and dynamic feeling of subsequent entries in the series, gave a real sense of progression as levelling up enabled my character to actually hit enemies and successfully cast what spells that had once felt far out of my depth. I don't have too many hours into the game just yet, but I've explored a great deal of the map and progressed into the main story and can't wait to play for many hours more. I would recommend this game to any Elder Scrolls fan with the caveat that they'll have to look past the game's lackluster, outdated exterior to find the truly excellent experience within. Despite what its most rabid fans will tell you, this game is by no means perfect. However, it is a blast to sink your teeth into and definitely worth your time.

I want to love this game with all my heart but i cant. Dont get me wrong this game is extremely enjoyable, The concept is great and addictive. Everything is perfect and fun untill it becomes more than its worth in terms of effort. At some point it bcomes apparent that the concept is muddied by the fact that you control every tiny aspect of the crew and their actions, which isnt a bad thing, but becomes harder than you think at first.
Here are some of the largest cons
Gunners:
The gunners will not fire at anything unless you spot it for them. This wouldnt be an issue if at some point later on they had some kind of skill that allowed them to at least respond to incoming fire solo. Instead they sit there and drool untill they die or you manage to spot a target for them.
The gunners do not learn any form of accuracy as they gain experience, Even the focus fire skill lead them to just hosing a specific area a fighter resides, only now they dont let off the trigger untill they run out of ammo of the skill runs out. this leads to later aces who maneuvers are sporadic patterns and passes being impossible to defend against.
Piloting:
The pilot will not move so much as an inch without you spotting a nav point or issueing the single evasion command. This means that the second an enemy BF110 gets under you, theres about 3 seconds to hit the corckscrew command before you lose every gunner in the tail. This command may or may not spike you into the ground and upon completion , this also leaves you manauverless for quite some time.  The slight ability to sway from side to side to mildly evade fire from below automatically or even adding just one more skill to aid with moving the largest target in the sky would help a lot.
Navigation:
No matter your level you wlll find you cannot go above low altitude, You're Navigator couldnt see the ground if he stood atop a ladder. There is no dynamic weather system allowing the option to use height on a clear day, Its just permanently cowdy. At high Altitude you can navigate by the stars but you wont get the chance before your crew freezes to death. Even with the addition of adequate therman clothing the lack of any ability for the navigator to see the ground or select a time of flight so they can nav by the stars leaves many grand slam missions a bust. You must drop from high altitude but the second you get close all markers cease, the navigator has recinded his directions and essentially becomes a usless member untill you drop to a low altitude at which the bomb is ineffective adn you fail the mission.
Missions:
Missions get repetative, moreso when you constantly lose bombers and crews and are more or less forced to grind the same route repeatedly untill you can get enough upgrades to attempt a campaign mission
The grind:
Heres where its interesting, its really a core concept to how the game itself is meant to be.Historically bomber losses were frequent, The constant need to build and recruit often to replace lost crews and planes is reflected in this game.
As long as you complete an objective you get the mney and research. You wont always make it home but you can try and refit the next bomber. The biggest issue is this gets increasngly frustrating and difficult as the campaign goes on. For instance i had a crew that somehow made it back for 28 missions and only lost two members. Im close to the end of the capaigns and i lost everything, All crew aboard were killed before the pilot went and the bomber fell out of the sky, now im back to square one.
This all makes sense and is one of the concepts i like in the game. I get fresh recruits. but they have the same skills as the early war men, No training improvements to ready them for the changes that you face currently. You're bomber is back to square one aswell. No factory fresh improvments for the year. This turns the learning curve into a cliff, pure luck might get this new un upgraded bomber back to base with at least 4 men alive. At this point the game stops,There is no real way to continue without constantly starting back over with the same stuff. There is no way around restarting, towards the end game, no matter how good your crew or aircraft has become. No matter your experienced crew or upgrades to the bomber every trip becomes one way. There is no return trip anymore and the fight turns iinto equipping the bomber to survive the 3-4 minutes till you can drop bombs
Personally i think the option for a new front, different bomber choices, ,more missions would make this cliff more palateble regardless of game progress. Rinse repeat is a tired trope and this is very barebones rinse repeat.
overall its an amazing concept, one in a million actually enjoyable game. but for the price i stales quicker than im willing to recomend.

The core concept is there. I'm a big fan of micro managing games. Especially when there's a lot going on at once. Coupled with the fact that your crew members can die instantly, it makes for an exciting, frustrating and rewarding system.
The problem is that your crew doesn't do anything on their own. Want to shoot down those planes? Gotta target them first or your gunners will just sit in the turret. Want to move towards the objective? Well target the nav point setup every 30 seconds and have your pilot follow it. Want to drop bombs? Well tell your bomber to get in the bay, open doors, select how many bombs and then release when you are over your target. Gunner's out of ammo? Well tell them to go get some more.
I didn't mind that there was no tactical pause where you could issue orders still while everything froze for a second. It made it much more intense. The problem is that there is so much to do at once that is easily overwhelming. All of this alongside your members having different abilities.
I played the first few missions over and over again getting decent gear and my crew leveled up before tackling the first "real" mission. I had to defend a friendly ship while it was torpedoed by submarines. Which wouldn't be so bad if it didn't tell me that I had 25 seconds to mark the submarine to fly over it, then watch my slow plane move there and drop a bomb. By that point I had 2 other enemy submarines launching torpedoes. The ship made it passed them with half hp and then it was attacked by coastal guns. So as soon as I managed to take out the first one, two more appeared on the map. Then the ship was destroyed and I was told to go back. I wasn't in any real danger either, it was just frustrating since there isn't a "fast" way to move or go places.
Overall it seemed like it could be a lot of fun. I had read the reviews and braced myself for a challenge. Knowing I could at least grind my guys and gear if needed. It just became a task of tediousness. Luckily I ended right at 2 hours played and was able to get a refund. Just know that within the first 90 minutes, you've seen everything there is to see and if you're not sure at that point about it, just refund it.

When I think of the kind of person who downvotes video game reviews that don't align with their own views, I think of the kind of person who made Gamergate a thing, and I feel sad. I also feel sad when I watch the end of Blade Runner, but for different reasons. This game is good and also extremely bad in a very specific and unfortunate way--I liked the story and voice work and could barely put up with any part of its gameplay. I'll give it a marginal blue happy thumb of positivity, but it's a damn close contest. This is called a review, in which I explain how this game was for -me-. It might be the same for you, and it might not. Know why? Consciousness is weird like that, and it exists in people other than you!
As a kid, I once resorted to calling up the Nintendo Power hotline to figure out how to get past a waterfall in Shadowgate Classic on the Game Boy Color. Over and over again, meanwhile reaping an exorbitant telephone charge from my parents, a counselor patiently explained to me that clicking Move and Waterfall on the word menu on-screen was not enough--I had to click Move, then the tiny sliver of space directly NEXT to the waterfall in order to get behind it. "Oh," I said, slowly. "Uhh, thanks!" There was absolutely no way I would have reached that conclusion on my own, because I had never been given reason to think that the interface allowed interaction with the scenes--I thought it was all about the word bank below.
Am I a born idiot? Am I so locked into my own way of thinking that I cannot conceive of different methods of function? You be the judge!
Yes, adventure point-and-click games are known for their obtuse puzzle moments, and The Fall contains what may be some of the worst cases I have ever seen having never touched a King's Quest. This is, based on my play and understanding of the story, an extremely intentional part of the game's narrative in which you play an AI OS on-board a high tech combat suit faced with having to think way, way, way the ♥♥♥♥ outside of any kind of conceptual box in order to protect the life of the unconscious human inside it. That's great! It makes a deeply atmospheric and genuinely moving and even sometimes challenging story of the horrifying paradoxes that make up a "functioning" autonomous mind.
Simultaneously, it plays like utter garbage, and the interface is so unfriendly I was rarely ever able to figure out the correct means of puzzling out anything across the entirety of the game in any sensible span of time. Even when I had to look at a walkthrough for solving the very first room I was not the slightest bit convinced that my failure to understand what the game wanted from me was in any way my fault. Room by room and puzzle by puzzle, The Fall willfully or accidentally misleads you to search for things that could solve puzzles, only to have you discover (in a walkthrough) that the things you expected to need might just be leftover red herrings from earlier versions of the same puzzle and have nothing to do with anything. This entire game, then, purely on the gameplay side of things, spends its entire runtime serving as its own tutorial for gameplay concepts that are used once and never later elaborated upon.
That being said, I will say that it is worth suffering through even if you're as stupid as I am. This is one of those nice little sci-fi titles with its heart in the right place and its sights on the sort of philosophical vistas that moved the authors of Dune and Ubik and so on and so forth. It's a good text of great ideas, and it sank its discursive teeth into me deep enough that there was still stuff to think about afterward, things to mourn, and stuff to look forward to. That, like any video game puzzle, is not an easy thing to do well.

Machinarium is a touching game that is just long enough to be refreshing but not long enough to get stale. The characters invoke emotion without words, the puzzles are fun, and the hint scheme is a fantastic middle ground between banging one's head against a wall and reading a walkthrough - just enough work that you don't instantly give up, but not so frustrating that you're driven off.
Also, it is great for kids. :)

Machinarium is an alternate universe puzzle point and click adventure in which you play as a small robot known as Josef who is looking for his missing girlfriend Berta. The adventure starts with you laying in a scrapheap figuring out how to piece yourself together. And once you get past that little puzzle, you quickly realise this is not an easy game... The puzzles are definitely more inline with the difficultly of the 16bit area of video gaming, not that it is a bad thing thing. The difficulty of the game naturally fits in with the aesthetics of the art, one can spend so long on certain puzzles, it gives plenty of time to admire the sheer beauty of the hand drawn art. The puzzles are creative and fresh, with a strong touch of quirkiness and humour with every completion. The music is easy on the ears and integrates with the games deep atmosphere. My criticisms of Machinarium would be that pointer can be a little imprecise, also if you move Josef while he is in tall or shot form, he hobbles along at a tedious pace. And the game does not offer any video settings, on certain monitors it can appear 'boxed'. Besides these minor setbacks, Machinarium is a beautiful work of art and a solid puzzle game full of humour, unique surprises and character. I strongly recommend this one.

The story of modern Resident Evil is a series of crude attempts at action gaming/RE fan service. Don't get me wrong, I'm a big RE fan, but when you make these games insanely shallow, they're hardly worth experiencing. Raccoon City was hastily thrown together and feels more like a free DLC than a standalone game. Karate-kickiinig zombies in four directions is kinda cool, but the novelty wears off quickly when you realize how awful the rest of the game is. Don't bother with Raccoon City, just wait for Resident Evil HD or check out Revelations.

This game gets a lot of negative reviews. Yes, it's on GFWL. Yes, the AI is horrible. You probably shouldn't get this game if all you want is single player because the AI will make you want to flip tables and you have three of them on your team.  You should, however, consider getting this game if you have friends to play with, because the coop is a ton of fun. You can move while aiming, lob various kinds of grenades, and you also have the chance to get infected when a zombie melees you which means you need to keep an antiviral on you (and keep an eye on friends if they're starting to turn. Everyone knows real friends kill their zombified friends. It's in the bro code). You can also start bleeding which will attract zombies to you. Mechanics such as these keep the gameplay interesting. The story is obviously not canon but it's a fun "what-if" scenario that features some familiar faces like Leon, Ada, Claire, and Carlos.  Although the characters you can play as (and there are quite a few to choose from, each with their own unique dialoges which adds replayability) are unknowns outside of this game, they all have distinct personalities and back stories. Sadly, a lot of the character details were cut from the game itself (for example, Dee-Ay's name comes the fact that he's actually a gay man and the letters stand for "Don't Ask," referencing the don't-ask-don't-tell policy, and Lupo is the single mother of four children), but they are still fun to get to know.
Overall, I find the gameplay fun with friends (having all 4 players taken up by humans is amazing, but even playing with just one friend is a fun experience) and definitely recommend giving it a chance. The main game can be found in various corners of the internet for around $10 but the Echo Six expansion cannot be (it has been argued that the expansion is better than the main campaign - whether or not this is true, the main game is short and the expansion is definitely longer and worth playing - you get the first mission free). I personally was not impressed with the DLC weapons and never use them, although the Cowboy Shotgun can be fun to mess with (my favorite load out is Beltway with a Riot Gun and the Sumarai Edge). The skins are nifty and fun if you have $3 to burn (I enjoy letting Beltway show the world his prosthetic leg, for example) but obviously are just skins and can easily be passed up.
Have fun blowing stuff up, chasing Leon, saving infected friends by killing and reviving them, running from the horde when you're gushing blood, and laughing at the over the top evilness of Umbrella.

Small World 2 is an extremely fun and constantly flowing game, similar to Risk.
Each player selects a combination of a Race and Power (which change every time you play), and then attempts to take over as much territory as possible on the map. The trick is that you'll only be able to push your Race so far, and will then have to put it in 'Decline,' which will allow it to continue earning you points while the pieces are still on the board. On your next turn you pick a new Race and Power combination, and start all over.
Conquest in this game is very simple, it requires a flat number of tokens plus an extra token for every item in the space - like a mountain token or another player's pieces. This keeps play fast and easy to decide your next move.
All in all, a great game for any board game fan or wannabe Ruler Of Everything The Light Touches.

Small World 2 is a tablet port of the board game "Small World", of critical acclaim.
Sadly, I cannot recommend this game, and warn those to proceed with trepedation.
The game feels as though it is meant to be played "once in a while", multiplayer, via e-mail with a friend. I say this because every single time you tab out of the game, if you are playing live, you need to watch the moves of those who played after your last turn over and over again. Every single time. Even if you tab out for a few seconds. What this boils down to is that if you and 4 friends are playing (as was our case) 80% of the time spent "playing" the game translates to watching back previous moves while you laboriously await your turn. This is hopefully something that could be patched/fixed, but as this is a direct port from a tablet variant I don't foresee this happening.
Next up, if you don't know how to play Small World, don't in any way expect this game to teach you. Thankfully, we had a seasoned pro of Small World playing with us so we had some idea what was going on, but the shear lack of tooltips, information and tutelage was kind of staggering. I'd say this is the type of game that is a) aimed towards someone who already plays Small World and b) a tablet device or phone.
The controls, the feel, and the entirity of the game just scream tablet game. And that's great! On a tablet. Sadly, as a PC title, it falls short.
After enduring one hour long game with my friends, I immediately requested a Steam refund for this severely underwhelming game, which was rejected as I'd already used the title, so for everyone else out there: beware.
The title has great promise! Small World is a GREAT board game, but this digital port just does not deliver. Maybe the devs will pick this up and adapt it, and if so I'll happily edit my review and re-review the title; after all, Small World itself is a great game! But for now, again, beware.

I normally wait ages to write a review, but I am going to swoop in on this one since I see a lot of reviews that are reviewing this game based on what it is not.
This game requires no pause function.  The theme of the game is the hectic and dangerous and amazing feats performed by the military personel who flew these type bombers in the war.  There is no pause.  I know, it is a game.  And the no pause is a key part of this game.  At least that is how I feel about it.
With a pause the game would be mediocre.  The no pause makes this game work.
Yes it gets a little crazy, and yes you will find yourself spinning cameras and clicking like a madman to keep up, and you will more than likely lose some crew, fail some missions.
But that is the fun!  Nothing feels more awesome than returning to base in a flaming plane with one engine and half the crew.  The game can be punishing, one false move (like telling your pilot to do an emergency dive while the mechanic is on the wing) can lead to disaster.  But it is also rewarding, there seems to be lots of gear to unlock, and the skills that I have seen unlock so far really ease down the 'craziness' as your crew levels up.  And once your navigator can set custom headings you can really take control of your flight path and take charge of more of the strategy.
It is a really fun game, kind of feels like FTL and Kerbal Space Program, without the ship design.  But the Gameplay is like FTL, and I don't know, maybe just the style, makes me think of Kerbal as my crew is crawling around the plane.
Anyways, long story short, this game is really good.  Fun little real time strategy game that seems quite deep for it's price and it's look, and so far, has me coming back for more.
If you get mad at games for being 'too hard' and demand there be a pause then you might want to stay away.  For every one else interested in this genre this game is a gem.  Great price point too.

Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game was made for me! Every ten minutes I giggled to myself saying "this game is amazing," and I'm not even being hyperbolic. I've been looking for a game exactly like this for years and I can't say how happy I am to finally get my wish.

These guys made a hell of a game.  The graphics scared me off at first because I typically don't like that art style, but in this game it absolutely works.  Despite what it looks like this isn't really a casual game, it is actually quite intense at times.  Sometimes you're on what is expected to be a low risk mission and you aren't paying attention for a few minutes and half your crew is dead from a heavy fighter with schrage musik blasting you from your underbelly where you carelessly didn't put a ventral gunner.  It is those missions, and the constant threat that make this game great.  Death can ALWAYS be avoided, but can't be undone, there's a memorial wall in the title screen for your crew memebers for a reason, and when you're new you might get a few names on it.  This game does a great job of rewarding people that think quickly and go in prepared.
Whatever you do, don't rush the campaign.  You will get a lot more difficult missions and not as many simple ones if you do, and you might not be prepared.  As you play you start getting more procedural and you start coming up with habits of keeping an eye on the enemy fighters and knowing where to put your gunners when, as well as prioritizing defence or just getting off your bombs ASAP, or even navigation which can often be a factor in later missions.
Despite some of the negative reviews, people that die a lot aren't left completely out to dry.  Sure some people get frustrated and rage quit if they lose thier progress, but keep in mind, research persists so you aren't starting over.  It is very possible to rebound from a total loss of crew and your plane, if the mission is too hard, the pilot has an option of aborting the mission (something the tutorial probably should have said).
Long story short, if you like crew managment games like FTL, World War 2, and games that get your heart racing sometimes, I would absolutely reccomend this game.

Lightning strikes down upon us, setting our village to flames. It reminds me of when I first saw that fire. I named it the red flower.
An object, completely circle towered above our feeble attempts to retreat. Bright red lights shone down onto my friends I had known since the beginning of my life. I looked away. I watched as everything and everyone I knew died in front of my eyes. It was horrible.
I somehow managed to survive that horrid day, I found the survivors and rebuilt our civilisation. We discovered many things that would aid us in our lives. We grew stronger and conquered our enemies.
We discovered a large metal cylinder inside one of our opponents buildings that were not nothing but dust. The cylinder opened, and I remembered. I remembered the day that my friends died. It was that flying monster, that horrible, horrible thing that killed us all. But I had to explore it.
Night was falling, and we had defeated every living thing that could possibly be a threat. No mercy. Just death. A thick fog blinded us as we made our way back to the spaceship. It towered above us yet again. The rest of my fellow friends stood beside me, and crowded around the ship. I opened the hatch and walked inside. I felt the eyes of many people watch closely as I disappeared into the darkness of the spaceship.
A whole new world surrounded me. It was amazing. I flew further out of the planets gravitational pull. Out of the solar system. I gazed over the white pretty lights sparkling and twinkling in front of me.
Then I saw it. Another person to defeat.
The enemy spaceship wizzed around me as I tried to find a way to fight back. BOOM! A missile hit the ship. The spaceship fell off course, and was aiming straight back to my planet. Those red lights punctured the ship and cut it in half.
I flailed helplessly as I was pulled out of the spaceship, still falling back to the planet. I realised that I was about to die. Tears fell down my cheeks as I choked without the oxygen I needed to live. I hoped I would pass out before I hit the surface of our barren planet that was ripped of resources by us.
I waited for my death. Closer and closer the planet came. Helplessly falling. Down and down. I remembered everyone I loved and knew, and felt sorry. I should of fought with them against the spaceship. Instead of being a coward and running. I should of fought, and not care if I died. At least I would go down as a hero.
Another single tear fell down my left cheek, and I hit the ground.

Although not exactly without its flaws, The Fall is a refreshing title that gives some diversity and quality into the gaming scene. It is definitely a unique game, that mixes platform and shooting genre with (you wont believe this) Point and Click adventure games.
The story is intriguing enough to get you started, and although the controls can seem a bit clunky, you'll get used to them (I played on a gamepad, but since there are some shooting sequences, K+M combo can also be a good solution). There is not much jumping going around anyway.
You will take on a role of ARID, an AI that is designed to protect her pilot host that is actually inside the suit. Since the pilot is injured from THE FALL, Arid will have to find a way to repair her diagnostic tools and some other non-working functions, and ensure the safety of the pilot.
This will lead to some very interesting situations, conflicts between AI's, dialogues about what is right or wrong, and their view on the world, with an emotionless logical way of thinking. For sure it is not the best game about this storywise, but it can pass. Ending gives a little more to the story and there is a sequel announced.
One more thing - if you are not a fan of thinking that hard when you play a game - think twice about buying this. It is not a hard game, but what u can't see from the screenshots is -  there is a lot of clue searching and item combining. Actually, that is the main element of the game. This is not a puzzle platformer, this is a P&C platformer (new genre?)
From me, definitely a big thumbs up, I didn't know what to expect from it, but I sure had a great time playing it. And kudos to the new genre :)

To preface this review and give everybody context, I have been playing Heroes & Generals since the beginning of the CBT - back whenever a majority of all players were from the EU - and have played on and off since the addition of more tanks. I am a scorned lover of this game. Heroes & Generals is a truly mediocre experience, with developers that - while intending well; are soul-crushingly incompetent. This game has seen me through many years, and through those years - I never once recall truly enjoying the game despite sinking money into it, to perhaps see the developers through in making a not♥♥♥♥♥♥experience.
***Note***: I want to love this game so badly, but it is such a terrible experience.
Balance is something very frequently brought up in this game, and has been since CBT whenever people would claim that the Germans don't deserve new content because of the MG42/MP40 (more recently, Allies and Slavs crying about the MP44/STG-44 while the Amerifats got the M1/M2 Carbine.); and the Allied players would whine and whinge about how "brokenly OP" the Germans are. This is due to the developers and playerbase noting that the Allies would never win (still don't, either) campaigns. Now, to the not brain-dead or blind player; this isn't an indication of weapon/vehicle quality, but merely a harsh truth. Allied players are bad at the game, this is a point I cannot emphasize enough. Having played both nations somewhat extensively (Allies in CBT, Germans afterwards), I can very, very easily dismiss any claims of the Germans being OP - if anything, they are far from it.
But, to return to the topic of the Allies never winning wars - this is simply due to the players that play the factions. They'll gladly wave arbitrary numbers in your face and scream "LOOK AT HOW OP THEY ARE!" while they plug their ears at the most minute of retorts. The Developers have tried extensively to give the Allies more weight in campaigns; and it has failed every single time due to none other than the playerbase.
In summary: Confirmation Bias + Whiney Kids + Incompetent Devs = OP Allies and Slavs.

H&G is in desperate need of more improvements to gameplay quality, balance, and physics; three things severely lacking from the game as of writing this (Post Baur, Pre Churchill). LESS WEAPONS AND VEHICLES, MORE MAPS AND GAMEMODES.

However, in turn; we have completely sub-par sound effects. Every weapon sounds completely and utterly fake, they sound like tin cans hitting eachother in the wind. Absolutely garbage.
On top of this, you have murky graphics with dull and cold colors everywhere. Not entirely a bad thing, and also not entirely without choice. The developers intentionally made the game gloomy, but this makes visuals poor and spotting difficult on certain maps in certain weather. But, simultaneously allows for more immersion.
The UI both in-game, and in the browser client are absolutely awful. Very basic, very uninspired. You cannot mess about in the browser client while in MM, and the Squad system is absolutely terrible and in dire need of reworking to be worthy of using more often than never.
This is my biggest point. This game has such a ♥♥♥♥ing terrible netcode and hit registry that it makes me want to kill myself. I swear to God, every time I participate in a battle; I feel like I might have a goddamn stroke or anueryism. This is due to numerous factors, but is mostly due to the developers sticking with non-dedicated, client-generated servers for matches (think Call of Duty, but with potentially slower hosts that make the game goddamn near unplayable.)
Optimization is fine, I've personally never experienced any problems with it - but I have a moderately high-end gamping computer; so it would have probably never have been an issue for me to begin with.

Heroes & Generals is a truly mediocre experience wherein♥♥♥♥♥♥hit detection, netcoding, balance, maps, map design, and a playerbase await you. I have no idea what to think about Amelon. I mean that in a good way, I think.
This game is one of the weirdest experiences I've ever had. It's an exploration game with a heavy emphasis on story, but the entire game feels like you are in somebody elses dream world.
The gameplay revolves around moving your robot to different areas on a map, getting some upgrades to move faster, but mostly you will be interacting with environments and talking to the various denizens of the robotic wasteland.
Mostly you will be exploring, solving a few puzzles and doing some branching dialogue.
I feel like the developer put a lot of effort into Amelon. It's obvious they are still learning due to how broken and janky many aspects are, but in this specific case it almost added to my experience.
The translated dialogue and voiceovers are bad, really bad. It sounds like the developer and a couple friends recorded it in their bedrooms and used Google Translate to get an English script. The audio levels are all over the place and everyone sounds the same.
There are many parts of the game that look unfinished, some animated cutscenes are more like visual storyboards and there are objects in the game entirely missing part of the render at the back.
It's difficult to comprehend the story, but from what I understand you are trying to recover some old memories and you used to be human but humanity went all Deus Ex and upgraded themselves out of their own body.
There are a lot of unexpected memes in the game that took me by surprise. I almost think the developer put them in their to say that after humanity is over, weird stuff on the internet remains but who knows. I am concerned about whether the developer has the rights to use some of these, particularly songs like "Friday". It's a weird scenario.
There's also an option to do a robot fart inside a post-apocalyptic theatre which I greatly enjoy.
Amelon is just so freaking weird that I oddly have to recommend it if you want a surreal experience and can handle extreme jank. It's almost fascinating.

Morrowind has to be one of the most aged, arduous games you could ever play. But it defined a whole generation and brought the Elder Scrolls series into the modern light. Combat is clunky but you can really feel your character grow as you begin to hit more things and face much tougher enemies. The Elder Scrolls has always included a massive world to explore but I think no game like it has ever invoked the true freedom of a players decisions like this one has.
The Spells and Enchantment's make anything possible in this game. Whereas other games in the series and in other open worlds have set resistrictions on the player. Morrowind's greatest strength is the ability to play how you want. You can enchant and craft leviation relics and spells to complely avoid areas, make items which drain the life of users who wear them (making killing civilians without being noticed a breeze) and practically create anything you can think of. Even the main story is something that can be overlooked or ruined completely if that is what you want to do.
Despite all of its flaws in gameplay, that is what makes Morrowind so special for me even today. It has problems and I certainly don't think its the best RPG ever made. But it's a captivating game with a rich lore and a true sense of freedom that even games today have trouble creating.
It's been a while since I've played this game. After playing Skyrim, I realized how rewarding this game is. It's tough, but it's worth it.

Morrowind won't hold your hand. It's dark and deep and the main story is much more complex than in Skyrim or Oblivion. There’s no “good” or “bad” here and it’s virtually impossible to make everyone love you. And this makes the game’s world truly believable.
Morrowind simply asks you to take your time, get into the lore, explore the world, understand its politics and history. It's a game that's hard to get into... but very satisfying when you do. Definitely not for everyone. Still, the atmosphere, the main story, the side quests, the politics, the alchemy and enchanting system and the overall freedom that Morrowind gives you make up for all its flaws.
If you're looking for an outlandish open-world RPG experience in a dark cruel world... I'd definitely recommend Morrowind. Here you need to earn your respect, slowly build up your reputation and only then you may truly enjoy it as a power fantasy game. And trust me, it'll give you much more satisfaction than being called the Dragonborn after 30 or 60 minutes of gameplay.

Let me be clear when I say that I really do enjoy playing "Resident Evil Operation Raccoon City", the game has in my opinion solid graphics and great game-play for both the single and multiplayer experience, but multiplayer can be a real blast and where the most fun can be had. Also for me finally being able to play as Umbrella and playing through franchise events through their perspective is a joy.
However if STEAM Reviews could be either rated as Positive/Neutral/Negative vs. just the choices of Positive/Negative I would put this review at "Neutral". As fun as this game can be I just can't fully recommend it at this time and here is why....
Why does STEAM still sell games that have "GAMES For WINDOWS LIVE", the support for that service has been stopped.
While there are people that would argue the GFWL service still works as it always has, I will tell you from experience that I have never had any issues until this year.
Sometimes this game will launch and work fine, other times it will need you to actually delete a settings file to launch or you will be forced to perform a clean install of the GFWL Client. It can be extremely frustrating and time consuming to resolve. There are people who own this game that cannot play because the game will not launch or it will crash at startup and this all is due to GFWL.
I never had problems with Games For Windows Live until they stopped support.
GFWL works but no one should not have to keep fixing this game or any game to play or just to launch without crashing, that really is just ridiculous. Honestly I wish I could count how many times I had re-downloaded the most current version of GFWL just to perform a fresh/clean install and even then the there was no guarantee that the game would work. Sometimes you will find that you might have to go to My Documents (C:\Users\Daniel\Documents\CAPCOM\RERC) and delete the Settings File just to get the game to launch without crashing, again this can be a frustrating experience.
If you decide to buy just understand what you may be getting yourself into, but also know that with the frequent STEAM sales you can get the complete pack for a very sweet price.

•	After the Install restart your PC once again, then sign into "Games For Windows Marketplace" at least once with a valid username and password or create one @
.

So once I finally got the game to semi recoginze my EA login I could start to play the game -
The game is esentialy 5 Games in one, the first 4 levels are shallow psudo-RTS, with a very shallow and basic concept. Start as a single cell organism, you can't die, and all this is is selecting if you want to be a herbivore, an ominvore, or a Carnivore.... Still fun and silly to look at. Next you select what traits you want to evolve - combat based (Biting, Spitting, Charging or Clubbing) or Charming traits (Singing, Dancing, Strutting and posing) with little mini games for either path, OK sort of fun. Then moving on the Tribes where you hunt and gather and more mini games on if you want to kill the next tribe over, or serenade them with Maracas, Digirido and flutes. Then a Very tedious RTS bit with invading (Relgiously converting or Trading with) cities. Yes you can customise your creature, but basicly most of the advantages become mute when you move on to the next level of the game.
So it is a shallow take on evelution, now my major problem with the game. It is broken at the Space bit, all the stars are called "BAD DATA" and all the planets in the stars are also called "BAD DATA". So when you get a mission go to BAD_DATA in the BAD_DATA system and bother some sort of creature. It is almost impossible to work out where to go. I get that the obsessing over the colour scheme and appearance of you creature might keep some entertained, that fact that they make no tangible difference to the game mechanic or to the increasingly dull game play, just isn't enough to keep me entertained.
So if you play multiple times, your previous creatures will pop up in later play throughs. This probably would give some novelty interest in later play throughs, but I don't think I can do that to my self.
I brought this 8 year old game on sale, for 12 NZ$ so about the cost of 6 beers, and I still feel had.
If you want vast space - Elite Dangerous. If you want a fun RTS, any other RTS will have more substance and above all fun - might I recomend Startopia, of Dungeon Keeper (or one of its many clones).
But this is best left to the mists of time as a nice idea really badly realised.

I thought I reviewed this previously. Anyway, Machinarium has a unique style, but doesn't hold up greatly these days. The primary issue is the reliance on Flash, making the game unstable and buggy. is one of the greatest adventures of this era. You play as a nameless hero who must propel themselves across the roofs of trucks and through obstacles to reach the finish line of each course.
It’s not quite that dramatic, but
is honestly a great time. It’s a pretty unique game that includes varied world types, fluid movement, and pure action with no filler. There’s something about fast-paced leaping from truck to truck that you can’t find in other games. Putting on some upbeat music and jumping around is pretty killer.
Levels vary in length and difficulty. You may complete some in only one or two tries, but others may have you stuck for many more. Even for levels I found myself having difficulties, the challenge never felt impossible.
is a game that you gradually improve at and as it ramps up the difficulty. Flying through a level with precision where you were previously failing within seconds is quite satisfying.
There are a handful of abilities to help you if needed. The vary in price (and I’m assuming usefulness) which you earn based on level scores. I played almost exclusively using double jump as my only ability, so I can’t really comment on how much effect the others have.
I think that
is best enjoyed in shorter bursts of play. It isn’t the longest game, so doing that helps extend the life a bit. It’s definitely replayable in terms of improving your stage score or trying out new abilities, as well as just being fun enough in general to redo levels. Seasonal worlds for Halloween & Christmas have been added in free updates and
also has Steam Workshop support.
While
is a blast to play, and I definitely recommend it, I would still suggest picking it up on a sale just because it’s a little on the shorter side.
(At the time of writing this, it’s currently available in the Humble Bundle for about ~$7.50 including other games. Definitely consider this if you’re interested!)

I have mixed feelings, but overall I think it's a worthwhile experience with some clever story-telling and memorable characters.  This is first and foremost an RPG, unlike the  second and third renditions; where combat feels more streamlined to a wider audience and variety of platform. [Consoles]  The best comparison I can think of from personal experience is the way the combat contrasted between Fallout 3 and 4.  The latter requiring more dexterity and aim instead of pure timing of clicks and proper use of combat styles.  In fact,  Witcher 1 may have more appeal to a classic dice-rolling RPGer; who-may enjoy knowing when and how to use the combination of styles, signs, and alchemy Geralt has at his disposal.
As far as the gameplay goes, well, that's where it gets figuratively and literally murky in my opinion.  I absolutely loved and hated the beginning of the game.  It was unrelenting and boring and yet somehow getting through it felt sort of rewarding by the end.  It starts to feel more tolerable; once you're done grinding it out in the mud n' muck of the early phase.
Some quests are eye-opening, but ultimately a waste of time in comparison to the real meat of the game. The characters are often brilliant, dark, and simulatenously comedic.  I'm still debating if all of the humor is intentional, but the antagonists' in this game are sometimes... Well, you'll see, oh yes, you'll see.  *cackles*
Witcher will challenge you and provide a sense of accomplishment.  I used to be an antagonist of companies putting arrows all over the mini-map - telling me exactly where to go - but I don't mind following a guidance system when time is of essence in my waking life.  Going back to the Witcher made me realize how much of gaming has evolved.  Fast travel?  Not quite.
Again, this is a more linear, classic RPG experience. This is an absolute positive for some even if it can sometimes be a nuisance or not as intuitive as modern games.
One could argue the ingenuity of our classic games are simply being reskinned and squeezed dry at the expense of the consumer.  Yes, no, and it depends on the game and obviously the preference of the player. There's some things in the newer games I prefer and some aspects to the older games I wouldn't mind seeing again - like difficulty. (Edit: Dark Souls I have not tried yet, but hear it fills this void for some.)  Reskinning isn't necessarily bad, either:  Imagine, Jedi Knight II with new graphics, yet the same core and addictive saber-battle gameplay.  The formula was balanced and fun. No need to reinvent the wheel there.  Will it make as much money?  Well, maybe not initially, but a good reputation and a game that has actual substance empowers a company and creates loyal fans instead.  Better to lose a bit now and have a legacy to be proud of later.
*casts Axii sign*  I knew you'd agree.
The hope is these games many grew up with and developers going into the industry are allowed room to breath and create a variety of games not constrained by the de facto or industry standards.
In other words, we're gonna need a Witcher!
Word of Caution:  It may go without saying, but if there ever was a M-rating appropriate game - this is it.  Not for the faint of heart or incredibly young.  Although, I find Geralt often has rational choices, and seems to convey a sort of morale lesson if one so chooses a more paragon path.  Geralt often comes across as the most compassionate character on the screen; if you are able to look past the blood dripping from his steel and silver.

Pros:
-You really feel like a super-hero/super-villian (yup, you pick it - you wanna be like Lex Luthor or Joker,  do it.  Complete with evil storyline).  Get the super speed and then upgrade it to level 1 and you will see what I mean, the building jumping is so unbelievably awesome (takes a bit to master), trust me, its worth downloading this game just to run around and do that.  It looks a LOT like The Flash TV show.  Do it, do it NOW.  Seriously.  It's freaking awesome.  No really.  Do it.  You're still reading.  Go.
-Complete customizable control of your character.  You pick the color (full palate with shading and brightness, triple custom!), you pick the heads, you pick the everything (wings, horns, spikes, tatoos, body size, rocky/flame/ice/plant/demon/etc skin, skirts, top hats, thigh highs, suits, if you can think of it, it's there - a little light on the close ups, but completely forgivable).  Once in game you can lock that, individually on each feature (including skin!), or continue to 'collect' styles as you find equipment.  You collect at a very nice rate.
-Your own customizable superhero lair.  A must for any good MMO.
-Challenging.  Not too hard, not too easy.  Really a great balance, and that is NOT something I say lightly.
-I saw at least one review that said nobody played it, that's wrong, as a new player I saw lots of people playing and had a nice balance of 'fighing for mobs' with also plenty of alone time.  Again, it was a nice balance.  I can see maybe how it's a bit light, but plenty of people play.  Again, I can't talk about end game.
-I'm a Marvel guy, and still I enjoyed it.
-Tutorial is good.
-The movement/transportation system in this game just blows away every MMO I have ever played.  You will get wherever you want to go really fast and almost immediately in the game.
-Solid MMO, I've played WoW and Wildstar in 1st tier guilds and played several others.  Maybe not some of the polishes of say a Wildstar, but this competes nicely given it's uniqueness.
-Huge spaces.  There is a lot to explore.
-Interesting storyline, familiar but new.
Cons:
-Its REALLY made for a controler.  All of the fighting combos are using the mouse1 and 2, which is not intuitive at all and difficult to master.  I haven't played long enough really, but there is a BIG learning curve for that on PC.
-It's most definitely NOT pay to play, however...you are very early on going to feel the pinch in your storage and progression on that issue.  You can NOT use your lair for anything but decoration until you pay - that is huge.  You can NOT add any more storage in the bank or your bags until you pay - doubly huge.  You can NOT save any cash beyond $1,500 - triple threat.  So while the actual action in the game doesn't require money, you are a force if you pay or not, the enjoyment of the game sufferes quite a bit if you don't do the monthly subscription.  $15/mo for a really polished unique game though, I mean what more are you looking for?
-It IS an older game at 2011, but it really doesn't feel like it.  The finishes are more than fine and will be for years.  But unless they continue to invest, it will most definitely become dated far sooner than some MMOs that are out there.
-I haven't seen a marketplace yet...maybe I haven't hit that point in the game?
-The crafting is fairly limited to just inserts for your equipment.  I think they really could do an awesome update with that.  This is also possibly a plus, because you're really not farming for much of anything, you're just beating up bad guys/good guys and getting equipment and costume upgrades.
-No vehicles, but you're a superhero, you don't need one.
