I think this game embodies almost every aspect of the point-and-click adventure genre, both positive and negative. Point-and-clicks are known for beautiful, often hand-drawn, character and background art, and as you can see from the trailer and screenshots. The genre hinges on having an interesting setting that the player will want to explore, and the rusty, robotic city of Machinarium fulfills that purpose wonderfully. However, the most infamous part of the genre is the puzzles, some of which were so unintuitive and infuriating that people often blame them from killing the genre. Machinarium has a variety of puzzles of different types, and it has some of the best deductive reasoning problems I’ve ever seen. Players will often times be presented with a machine, and they must use trial and error to learn what each button and lever does. However, for every one or two brilliant puzzles, there is an infuriating pixel hunt that drags the game down.
Also the demo of the game is a tad misleading. During the demo, the player will be confined to a small area with a clever deductive reasoning problem. While the best moments of the full game are like this, you will also have to deal with moments when you must backtrack through areas you have already been to find that one item that blends in with the background. In other words, the demo only represents the good parts of the game, so if you don’t care for the demo, you won’t like the full version. However, if you are willing to keep a walkthrough open in your web browser for the unintuitive puzzles, you can have a really excellent time in Machinarium

HuniePop is an adult-themed dating simulation crossed with a match-three game.
Note: HuniePop is definitely an adults-only game. There's an uncensor patch freely available, but even without that there is nudity in a sexual context.
The graphics are excellent. Each of the girls in the game is beautifully drawn to reflect their different personalities and the gallery art is mostly very nice, although can be somewhat crude in some instances. Multiple costumes and hairstyles are unlockable, too, providing a bit of variation for each encounter.
The interface is clear and colourful, with some pretty location backgrounds and a huge range of gifts to give to your dates.
The date interface (the match-three part of the game) is clear and easy to understand as well, and the 'ghosting' of objects showing the gems that will move when you drag a gem around in the game is a nice, helpful addition.
Music is fairly typical of the anime dating sim and visual novel genre. I didn't find it annoying, but I also wouldn't ever listen to it outside of the game. Sound effects are suitable, with the usual bleeps and sparkly sounds when matches are made during dates.
The game is professionally voiced, with each woman having a unique style, and the quality is excellent. Before I started the game I wasn't expecting this, and in my opinion the voices are very well done.
The objective of HuniePop is to date each of the women in the game and ultimately sleep with them. Where it differs from other dating simulation games, though, is in the actions required once you actually take one of the girls on a date: in order for the date to go well, you have to win a match-three style minigame.
The match-three aspect, too, is a little different from what you might have seen before, with each icon or gem colour representing a different personality trait, and each girl having a preference for a particular gem colour (and a dislike of another), making for an uneven distribution of points for each colour. One gem colour (Passion) builds up a multiplier for the other colours, and still another (Sentiment) provides access to special abilities that are unlocked by giving certain gifts to the girls. Finally, each game has a limited number of moves in which you must reach a certain points threshold, which increases significantly with each subsequent date.
It's all very well thought out and balanced, and makes the match-three dates much more tactical than you would at first expect.
The social (pre-date) part of the game includes a plethora of gifts to give to each girl, and titbits of information to learn about her. These provide a currency, of sorts, that can be used to upgrade your abilities in the match-three dates.
The writing quality is excellent, although the style may well put some players off. It all seems pretty misogynistic -- even if you play a girl -- and coarse, but I confess to laughing out loud at some of Kyu's comments. She's great!
Pros:
+ Kyu
+ Gorgeous anime girls
+ Excellent voices
+ Excellent writing, although the style may put some off
+ Uncensor patch available (if you're into that sort of thing)
+ Trading cards
+ Steam achievements
Cons:
- The match-three threshold increases slightly too quickly for my liking
- Too addictive by far!
HuniePop is a very professional game and is very addictive.
Recommended if you're into pretty anime girls and don't mind a bit of adult content.

I haven't finished a game in a long time, but The Fall took hold of me and wouldn't let me go till the end. It took me 6 hours, but I did get stuck a couple of times (really my fault since the puzzles for the most part are pretty logical), so I imagine there are plenty of first time players who will get through it in 3 or 4. I'd describe the game as a point and click adventure game without the point and click and light action elements. Instead of using the mouse cursor, you use your flashlight to point at objects (I used a gamepad which works nicely) and interact with them.
The best part of this game is the incredible atmosphere and story and how well they integrate with the gameplay elements. You play an AI aboard an advanced combat suite who seems to be desperately trying to rescue the human pilot inside. One of the more innovative ideas is that you must work within your operation programming in order to achieve your goals and, in some cases, do things that may seem on the surface to be a violation of your programming directives, but may be necessary to achieve your greater purpose. There are plenty of twists and turns and despite the fact that most of the characters you encounter in the game are also AI, they were anything but flat.
The combat seems mostly pointless and can get repetitive at times, but I still found it a nice break from solving puzzles. The only disappointment I have with the game is that it was short and some of your capabilities were only used once or twice throughout the whole experience.
Overall, 8/10 and can't wait for the sequel!

This game is awful. It's impossible to understand how there could be so many positive reviews, because the people making this game either hated their customers or have no clue how to code a video game.
First off, the combat is garbage. It is the most tedious and boring thing you can imagine. While there are multiple fighting styles, you will rarely use them, because the code of this game is awful. For example, no matter how high you increase your hit percentage, the strong style will never land a hit on anything but slow enemy types, or which there are few. Usually, slow enemy types come in groups, so you will mostly be using group style in these situations. Unless you exploit the awful coding of the game, in which case, you can wait for enemies to enter an animation and then use strong style, because for whatever reason, entering animation completely changes the forumla used to determine a hit -- this is stupid, because as it turns out in real life, the worst time to try hitting someone is when they are hitting you. It's astounding that a glitch like this never got fixed.
You can see other examples of how bad these developers were in the animation cancelling that frequently occurs in combat, where getting attacked by multiple enemies and moving slightly for position (two things that happen all the time in the game) can render your character useless and completely unresponsive to any commands. And they made a sequel to this.
Do you value your time? This game doesn't. In fact, it doesn't think very highly of you at all. Enemies can put you in a combat state by looking at you from halfway across the bland and boring maps, at which point you will be unable to use a door or loot a corpse while you wait for them to chase you for all of eternity. Combat with even trash enemies that you long outlevelled takes just as long as when the enemies were harder, in many cases requiring the same amount of sword swings even after you've stacked talents that should have made you more powerful. It's hard to tell why, because the game goes out of its way to make all the data you see on screen as small and missable as possible, putting damage totals too high above the enemies so you can't read them and engage in combat -- the cursor has to point at the enemy to hit them, which usually involves looking down. Frequently, you will find yourself unable to target a nearly dead enemy because another enemy behind you is grabbing every click, and yet not dying because you are swinging at it while facing the wrong direction.
Combat takes way too long to end, forcing you to wait to loot corpses or even walk through the giant entrace to a cave. Huh? Looting is tedious and boring, and there are way more ingredients in this game than you will ever need. The whole idea of potions in this game are a joke. You rarely face any substantial amount of enemies and after the first chapter, you have to rest long periods of time to get enemies to respawn, which means that the 4 hour potion you drank isn't going to last more than one round of grinding -- a complete waste.
Running is a joke. 90% of the people I encounter in a normal day walk faster than Geralt runs. Why didn't they make him just walk at a normal speed and add in a run ability? A few hours into the game, you'll realize they did it this way because there is very little actual good content in this game, and that most of your time will be spend running between your item storage, a campfire, and quest giver locations on various fetch quests, most of which have clearly been designed to force you to go the most possible distance.
A lot of the problems with this game remind me of a similarly broken, overhyped game, Stalker. Much like in that game, you will find that most of the crap you pick up, as well as most of the upgrades you find, are useless, serving only to waste your time collecting the junk and then waste more time managing your inventory.
This company should have hired someone to test this game, and should have made some effort to understand how reality works. Anyone who claims they tested this game but left the astounding post-combat delay in the game is either a liar or is just ignorant. There's no good reason why any developer on earth would ever make it so the computer tells you that you can't use the giant mouth of the cave exit because you are in combat when every single enemy in the entire environment is dead. My computer can perform a disgusting amount of calculations in an amount of time that I can't even fathom, because it's so short. These developers were unable to write a piece of software that can accurately check whether an enemy is dead or not. The fact that this level of incompetence was rewarded with 2 sequels is stupendously unbelievable.

Brief summary:
Original War is an RTS with a look that feels old but not Dated due to its style that focuses highly around the story and characters. each mission if you lose a character the character is gone for good (except if a bug occurs in character selection on one or two of the last missions) so keeping your men alive is key.
Story (few spoilers as possible):
The story in it is kinda simple but complex without trying to give spoilers. During WWII America finds an alien artifact. after years of research and naming it EON they find crystals in Siberia of a similar nature to EON and look into both. they soon discover EON is a device that can send anything placed within, back in time, using the crystals now named Siberite. most of the Siberite is in Russian turf though so to solve this they send soldiers back in time 2 billion years in the past to transfer the Siberite over to Alaska. when they get there they find resistance however. The Russians are ready and waiting from them.
Downsides:
The sounds can get a little aggravating if you're not used to them. basically get used to hearing "FINE SIR!" or "OKAY SIR!" every time you move a unit, in a high pitched voice most of the time.  ocasionally there's a bit of bad voice acting too albeit most is pretty good. there are a few missions in the game where if you do not know what you're doing or haven't done the mission 50 bazzilion times before like i have it can be VERY difficult even on easy mode. The only ones really to note though are the ones where you join the Alliance so if you're not planning to its not a bother. Unfortionatley due to the game being fairly obscure most of the multiplayer is empty unless you can get a friend to tag along with you. the final downside is that the game Lacks a skirmish mode or an offline non-story mode. it would of benefitted greatly from it due to it being so hard to find a multiplayer opponent.
Brief background summary:
Original war is a game that proves even rushed games on low budget can be good. the company was starting to go bankrupt near the end of the game's completion so it was all they could do to quickly get the game out before they did. As the company that made it is not around to maintain it, the game has become community run and there's even projects to get a third campaign currently underway by people who want to see the game more known. There's alot of modding from the community too if you can find them. some such as a third Arabian campaign albeit short an unfinished and ones that let you do a skirmish mode as the game lacks one itself as i said previously.
Conclusion:
I would highly recommend it because the story is interesting, the gameplay is fun, the soundtrack is pretty good and overall it can be a great experience. If you like old games, obscure games or retro games then I would say you get this game in a heartbreat. for those just looking for a fun RTS I still highly reccomend it but i feel its worth looking at before you get it to see if you like it.

Most definitely one of my bigest gaming loves.
And that is more then well deserved position! OW is (even thought it´s age) original not just in the means of timetravel and war in the far past and for the past. Above all it´s brilliant combination of rts and rpg, what makes it so unique. In terms of gameplay it means you have to care about every soldier you have (and in this harsh environment, it´s usually much less than optimal numbuer). You have to always think abut for what to use each soul and how to treat it. What skills to train, where to allocate the manpower, what technology develop and when. Becouse even won battle for valuable resource, if it took too much time, can endanger development of your base and therefore whole mission. Loosing any soldier means hell of a trouble. There are usually multiple ways how to achieve your goals, but every one need careful tactical thinking from base management to field battle strategy.
This way it may sound like hardcore stuff for very patient tacticians... but it´s not. Above all, it´s very enjoyable game for anybody. The main experience isn´t frustration, but fun. Lots of fun. There are some things that help this outcome. First is excellent level design. Missions arent repetitive, but almost always bring some new challenge. They vary from more traditional base-to-base war to Commandos-like stealth action. Often there are also twists in the developement of events, which boosts gameplay with dynamics and pushes you to be prepared for anything.
The last but not least quality is the main story. From the "cliché" of American-Russian war (just situated in unorthodox setting), situation quickly extends to be more complicated. Player is therefore forced to choose which side (and which politcs, ethics and philosophy) to pledge allegience to. Not just from global perspective, but from personal view of main hero and his relationships, too. Which even adds emotinal touch to game. Quite special for rts, isn´t it? Oh, I forgot to mention that (living) soldiers and their valuable experience goes to next missions. And that for some of the more important characters amongst them, you will soon develop special feeling.
Game has, of course, it´s weaknesses (like poor voicecast), but there are not many of them. Somebody may despise the old graphics, but I like it even after all those years.
So in the end I have only one advice regarding Original War: Enjoy It!!!

Longer time ago an American expedition found in Siberia a strange artefact called EON. After some time scientists found it’s a time machine. For using EON there was necessary a fuel called Siberite. However there was one problem - all supplies of Siberite were in Siberia, in Russia. That’s why Americans decided to send an expedition 2 milions years to the past and all supplies of Siberite move from Siberia to Alaska (that time they were connected). Then would be changed the space continuum and all Siberite would be in USA one day. But the Americans weren’t the only ones, who got this idea...
Original war is a real-time strategy with strong elements of RPG. The game was after it’s release (incorrectly) compared with Red Alert 2, but OW is pretty different game. There you have limited characters and every of them has own identity and skills that you can improve during missions. Often you can choose your favourite characters for your team the mission starts. If there dies any of your person, you will not be able to “reborn” him or her again. So, it’s not a strategy where you can buy hordes of soldiers and then you would crush the enemy by massive force. There you need to find the way how to defeat often stronger or better stationed enemy.
+ very original game (original war should be original =)) and interesting story
+ nice graphic (at least for year 2001)
+ campaigns are long and nonlinear (player has to make many decisions that can influence the story and the end as well)
+ three playable sides (Americans, Russians and later Aliance) and one additional (Arabians)

+ prehistoric animals

+ includes multiplayer (you can play there for Americans, Russians and Arabians too)

- no skirmish mode

I'm not great at doing thourough reviews but i i'll try and break it down
Game Play:
Fantastic! apart from maybe TERA this game has one of the best combat systems i've seen in an MMO, no only do you have the various skills your weapon combo's open up you also have a skill bar to access more definitive power abilities.
If you like player a healer in MMOs this game allows you to still be part of the fight while healing your teammates (since you gain your power resource by attacking) although a little simplistic with heals/buffs automatically going to the most injured player. This game also incorperates an active block system which every "class" you choose has to try and reduce incoming damage (and even causes a stun when used at the right time).
Crowd Controll in this game also feels unique with your block button also being a way to break out of CC so its not a difinitive you've now been taken out of the fight most of the time it depends on how fast you react to the controlling effect with even "classes" having a dedicated controller roll.
F2P:
Yeah alot of people may be put off by this especially with the ingame cash shop but apart from DLC content i never felt restricted compared to other players or weaker in anyway, okay it may be faster to get through the game content if you're paying for it but it's all still available to you if anything i felt i was gearing up too fast once i hit the cap so i never felt like this game was "pay to win".
Cons: Okay not paying the monthly fee is kind of a pain in the butt when you're limited to a 2000 in-game cash limit but when it comes to buying the gear you need none of it has a cost more than the free players can get because it is also usually coupled with a dungeon/raid resource you gather.
Not very challenging game once you've got a good idea of what you're doing you'll rarely find a major problem with a boss/enemy unless you have a whole group of inexperienced people but although there isn't "Much" of a challenge is still is possible to fail and it still does feel nice when you start clearing the higher tiers
but overall say you decided to buy a DLC for a power type you want to play the game for i'd say you'd definately get your moneys worth of entertainment out of it but it does feel like an MMO you come back to during dry spells but very fun nontheless

is a sad short story that takes about 5 minutes to complete.  It involves a parental mammoth looking for its children and reuniting with its herd, sadly, only tragedy awaits it when success seems to be within reach.

The voice-actress playing the narrator also does a great job at telling the story.
Some may complain that this game is too short, but given the story to be told, I feel it's ideal as it leaves no stone unturned and no loose ends.  It's honestly hard to find any problems with this title nor can I recommend any improvements.

HuniePop is an adult-themed dating simulation crossed with a match-three game.
Note: HuniePop is definitely an adults-only game. There's an uncensor patch freely available, but even without that there is nudity in a sexual context.
The graphics are excellent. Each of the girls in the game is beautifully drawn to reflect their different personalities and the gallery art is mostly very nice, although can be somewhat crude in some instances. Multiple costumes and hairstyles are unlockable, too, providing a bit of variation for each encounter.
The interface is clear and colourful, with some pretty location backgrounds and a huge range of gifts to give to your dates.
The date interface (the match-three part of the game) is clear and easy to understand as well, and the 'ghosting' of objects showing the gems that will move when you drag a gem around in the game is a nice, helpful addition.
Music is fairly typical of the anime dating sim and visual novel genre. I didn't find it annoying, but I also wouldn't ever listen to it outside of the game. Sound effects are suitable, with the usual bleeps and sparkly sounds when matches are made during dates.
The game is professionally voiced, with each woman having a unique style, and the quality is excellent. Before I started the game I wasn't expecting this, and in my opinion the voices are very well done.
The objective of HuniePop is to date each of the women in the game and ultimately sleep with them. Where it differs from other dating simulation games, though, is in the actions required once you actually take one of the girls on a date: in order for the date to go well, you have to win a match-three style minigame.
The match-three aspect, too, is a little different from what you might have seen before, with each icon or gem colour representing a different personality trait, and each girl having a preference for a particular gem colour (and a dislike of another), making for an uneven distribution of points for each colour. One gem colour (Passion) builds up a multiplier for the other colours, and still another (Sentiment) provides access to special abilities that are unlocked by giving certain gifts to the girls. Finally, each game has a limited number of moves in which you must reach a certain points threshold, which increases significantly with each subsequent date.
It's all very well thought out and balanced, and makes the match-three dates much more tactical than you would at first expect.
The social (pre-date) part of the game includes a plethora of gifts to give to each girl, and titbits of information to learn about her. These provide a currency, of sorts, that can be used to upgrade your abilities in the match-three dates.
The writing quality is excellent, although the style may well put some players off. It all seems pretty misogynistic -- even if you play a girl -- and coarse, but I confess to laughing out loud at some of Kyu's comments. She's great!
Pros:
+ Kyu
+ Gorgeous anime girls
+ Excellent voices
+ Excellent writing, although the style may put some off
+ Uncensor patch available (if you're into that sort of thing)
+ Trading cards
+ Steam achievements
Cons:
- The match-three threshold increases slightly too quickly for my liking
- Too addictive by far!
HuniePop is a very professional game and is very addictive.
Recommended if you're into pretty anime girls and don't mind a bit of adult content.

Cubic Castles is a voxel-styled building MMO, where you can possess a realm of your own that you can build on.
First thing I'd like to point out, is that not everything is bought with your wallet. And even if it is, you can get 1,000 cubics for just 99cents. That's more than enough for these "housing packs" or whatever. The only things that I noticed that are store bought only are extra rooms, castle skins, character clothing (Some you can craft.) and some parkour realm necesseties. (Checkpoints and health blocks) However, you can earn these cubics anyway, even if it's at a slower pace. If you're dedicated, you can mow in those cubics. If not, heck ,there's coupon codes you can try and look out for to get 1k-2k cubics. Everything besides what I mentioned can be earned by crafting.
Server problems have gotten better. I noticed the top reviews were ones made on the day of the release. How could you expect server issues to be in tip top shape with the large influx of new players coming in? I for one had an account-specific issue once, and it fixed itself in a couple hours. It didn't happen again. This game is sure to continuously get better over time.
If you don't want to spend your precious cubics on an extra room, or on sentries to keep your chest safe, block them. Make sure your building privacy is setting to you and/or your trusted, and put all your important stuff in a shell of blocks so strangers can't steal anything.
TLDR; This game allows you to craft and get 95% of everything it offers, and it will continuously get better. Also, block your chests. What else could you want from a F2P game?

I do recommend this game, because it's a metric shxt-ton of fun, even on the free2play model.
The thing is, it really is "pay 2 win," or more like "pay-to-play-with-unhindered-progress."
Don't get me wrong, you can get very far for free and even keep playing for free and still have tons of fun, you just won't progress as quickly or efficiently as those that pay (the metaphorical glass ceiling).  What I mean by that is once you get to lvl 30, you'll see that the mods to increase your combat rating for the armor you purchase (with marks of triumph, not actual cash) are conveniently priced outside the amount of money your character can hold at a given time, and you'll be waiting for the ever-so-rare drop from a raid so you can craft the mod you need to increase your combat rating.  Subscribe, and you can purchase these mods from vendors and craft away.  To add insult to injury, you craft these mods with exobits that are scattered throughout the game, and you'll need 8 to make a byte, or a combination of 4 of any 2 types to create a hybrid.  If you subscribe you can purchase these on the auction, but as a free player or even premium (see below) you'll never be able to purchase them because other players price stacks of them to the tune of hundreds of thousands of dollars.
If you plan on playing for free, there is a 1k cash cap and an inventory cap, but if you spend as little as 5 bucks you can carry another 1k for a total of 2k and you get an expanded inventory slot.
The number of powers you have are limited, but you can unlock them if you buy whatever expansion packs, but that's not recommended.  If you're gonna spend any money at all, you may as well spend the 10 bucks a month and subscribe and get the unlimited cash wallet, expanded inventory slot, and access to all the DLC and powers.  Otherwise you'll end up spending some damn good money on the game (Like that 30 dollar DLC pack) with none of the perks of the subscription access.
To conclude, you will have a ton of fun, even for free.  The pay to win model isn't so much a pay to win model as it is a pay-to-play-with-unhindered-progress model.

If you love a good B-Movie, strategy games, and retro gaming experiences... this is an easy must buy.
The game has aged poorly, the online is pretty much dead & is a chore to be a part of, and there is a handful of bugs with the actual game. How on Earth can someone recommend this game?
First off, this game has a good storyline that has player make decisions, some of them that changes the game and are important. Imagine the story that's terribly cliche, a powerful resource that the most powerful individuals want control of, but the are in the territory of a country or territory they have no control over, but you just happen to have a time machine... what do you do?
The answer, you travel back in time to move this resource into an area you do have control over so that, in the future, you can have a boat load of these resources. In the American campagin, your goal is to travel back in time before man to move this resource that you call Siberite from Siberia to Alaska. This way, you control the resource in the future. The setup? The Russians that don't belong in the same era anymore than you insists it's called Alaskite and would prefer you all move it to Siberia. With two different futures, these forces clash to fight for this so powerful resources and, more importantly to the soldiers, because they're simply ordered to. You probably have already guessed what the storyline for the Russian campaign is.
There is drama throughout the storyline for both campaigns. Some characters have a personality that is likable, some not so much, and you develop newer technology as time goes by to fight the enemy. To really reveal anything more is a spoiler, but the story isn't exactly super amazing anyways.
The gameplay is addictive. Anyone that likes old school strategy games will understand the value of this game. Each soldier is inexpendable, you do not have the ability to create more and each man lost is an actual loss. There is no getting these individuals back, they're dead. Each vehicle requires a driver unless you design them to be AI controlled, which has some draw backs for either choice. Each structure requires people to man it. Even defensive towers require people to man them unless, again, you make them AI controled which does have draw back. Your people, they're all important. The most important character is you, the main protagonist for the campaign. You must survive, or it is a mission failure and it's time to start over.
With your people, you need to gather resources of three types to maintain your base. With these resources, you develop your base, vehicles, and the likes in order to maintain a feasible stance on the battlefield. You have to research technologies and abilities, you have to upgrade structures, you have to constantly improve yourself to maintain equal grounds, or even the advantage, with your opponents. Top it off, there is RPG elements that each individual person can improve which changes the difficulty of all these tasks, making it important which individual you use for each task.
The soundtrack is pretty good, too. Graphics are not too shabby either. There is a lot of charm in this game even for today's standards. The modding capabillity is as simple as early Command & Conquer games too, so you'll find plenty of mods to keep it fresh if you like!
So, it's a great game for a 2001 title. What are the draw backs?
Well, it's terribly dated. There was a time when RPG elements in an RTS was rare. There was a time when soldiers that perma die and cannot be replaced was rare. Today, there is plenty with both of these. This is now nothing special.
There is also the lack of good voice acting, or at least for the English version. I have heard that it's better in another language, but I only speak English so that's no good for me. If you cannot withstand B-Movie material, get ready to cringe. Additionally, some of the drama in the storyline can feel a bit empty or pointless when attempting to develop character depth.
There is also a handful of bugs, which OWSupport is infrequently fixing. They used to be super active, but I have no clue as of now if this is still the case. Some problems include structures originally controled by AI in campaign can be captured, but they still auto build vehicles and such. There is also this terribly consistent frame rate slowdown that happens, as far as I can tell, randomly for at the very least Windows 7 users which I would report, but what exactly would I say other than "so, there's a problem. I cannot tell you the cause of it, but good luck fixing it."
There is no singleplayer skirmish options, it's currently online or nothing if you don't wish to play the campaign. There is stories of mods being made, but I have not seen anything for I did not really look for it.
There is this feature for the campaign where each time you complete a mission, it creates a tree under it. This is nifty, because every choice you make or every soldier lost will progress and make a difference, so if you replay a mission and made changes, it will create a new progression with a new branch. However, you cannot name these trees, so you will need to remember which is which.
There is also a handful of dated issues. For example, you need to bulldoze down trees for base space, but you need to left click EVERY tree. There is also some lack in control when navigating around the battlefield unlike modern strategy games that give you a huge variety of ways to move the screen. This is an old game, if you're familiar with old RTS games, you'll know what to suspect.
Overall, this is a great game for its asking price. If you wish to play it online, you will need to do some research on it. It's doable though. For singleplayer, it's a good experience. It's not too terribly long, it has a good amount of depth for its duration, it will bring no tears in your eyes but it's enjoyable.
I think that due to the fact I played this game actively since 2003, I have a bit of a bias for this game. So it's difficult to realisticly rate it out of 10. I think that, in general, it deserves 7/10, but a part of me feels that is a bit low for what it really deserves.
Pros-
Good story
Good soundtrack
Great Balance
RPG elements, perma death, in game choices matter
Online and Mod community does exist, even if it is very small
Most of the bugs from 2001 are gone and they're infrequently fixing more of them.
The ♥♥♥♥ing price, especially on sales, is very good.
Cons-
Acting is terrible, some of the storyline's drama is a bit cliche or boring, or meaningless to players
There is some bugs still present, though they're very few in number they are also very noticable.
It's a chore to play online, from port forwarding to running a third party software.
It has some dated problems that probably will not be changed.
*for modders* there is a lot of hardcoded issues that simply cannot be changed due to menu sizes and such, so there isn't a whole lot beyond different campaigns you can really do.

I don't even know where to begin.
Everything about this game is fantastic.  The music is fantastic.  The art is fantastic.  The point-and-click gameplay is fantastic.  This game is wonderful.
Prepare to be drawn in by the surreal and enveloping atmosphere of Machinarium.  It's pretty standard point-and-click gameplay, but very well done.  Many many areas to visit and explore, tons of puzzles to solve, and a vague but charming narrative that unfolds as you progress.
I can't recommend this game enough.  It's an experience.

Gameplay: The story is adorable and is completely communicated through pictures and scenes. There are clever solutions to many of the problems, and if you run into trouble you can play a mini-game that takes you long enough to be discouraged to use it, but not torturous if you are legitimately stuck.
Visuals: The style is very detailed and seems like every scene was painted purposefully. This game is certainly easy to look at for the entirety of the play through.
Audio: The sound track for this game is absolutely fantastic. Not only does it insert you into the scene's, it's also good to listen to on its own. I often use it as my background music for studying.
Replayability*: This is a hard one to verbalize. If you wait before you play the game a second time, you'll most likely forget the placement of all the solutions, but the story will still be stale, and a lot of the fun is in the story. This game lasted me 6 hours of fun, but I seldom pick it up again.
Point where I'd say you have to buy it: $2.50
*This varies A LOT from person to person, so only rely on this category from me if you've agreed with my other reviews' replayability sections.

Only get if you're into this kind of thing (or want to try something new).
It took me less than 2 hours to get 100% of achievements.

There isn't any.
There's no goal, no endgame, it's just flying. For fun.
The maps are pretty and they serve the main purpose of the game - relaxation - very well.
With procedural generation, they look different each time, even though they are built with the same components.
It's awesome! I've never had a chance to fly a real wingsuit, but this is exactly how I hope it would feel like.
I've mostly played with a controller and it was great. I checked out keyboard too and it was good enough. Controller feels more natural, but if you prefer a keyboard, you'll be fine too.
There's no music here, just the whooshing sound of air when you're flying. And the occasional crash noise.
There are two game modes.
First one is competitive - you get points for flying close to structures. The closer you fly by, the more points you get. And you have to beat your high score.
The second one is called Zen - all the HUD notifications are disabled. You don't have to worry about points, multipliers or anything else. You just fly, enjoy the view and try to relax.
One feature worth mentioning here is the procedural generation. Yes, I've said it before, it's there. But the cool thing about it is that each map is generated based on a seed number. That means when you encounter a map that you like, you can save its seed and regenerate the same map whenever you want. Or you can share that seed with your friends or anyone else, so they can try to beat your score on the exact same map.
I've played this game for two hours and that was time well spent.
But I don't think I'm gonna be playing it much more than that.
- relaxing
- pretty, procedurally generated maps
- seed numbers, allowing to exchange maps with friends
- no endgame
- nothing to do after 2 hours

Are you stressed, bored or you've got work to do but you wanna take a break and play something? Then Superflight is the game you are looking for.

Since it is not a linear game, you can go wherever you want in the map, so if you are stuck, just go somewhere else in the map.
It's a simple game for your simple needs. Run the game, relax a bit then get back to work, or whatever you are doing.

The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind is a classic Open World RPG. It allows you freedom to do what you wish, go where you choose, right after you complete the intro. It won't hold your hand, or coddle you though, so you have to play smartly... wander too far in the wrong direction and you may find yourself getting chomped or blown to bits by something way too powerful for you. You could spend over 100 hours in this game and find half of what lies within it's world.  The characters, plot, and background lore are all carefully crafted, within a vast, rich wold.

There was quite a bit that I found fantastic in this game, and other things that really bothered me. (opinion based)
Pros: Fantastic customization. You get to make the hero you want with few limitations. Gameplay is action oriented. No auto attack or click and hold to attack. Moves revolve around skills and combos.  The game is fully explorable. Almost open world (with the exceptions of changing cities, going in buildings, and doing dungeons). You can have a hideout, but that seems to be more for those willing to spend money (furnishings, better locations). I never talked much, but, from what I could tell (back when I still played) the community was very active. Questing: It does have your filler quests to lengthen the game and provide quest gear, but the story quests are fun, and bosses can be difficult (because why have a game if it is too easy?).
Cons: As an MMO, I expect this, but it still bugs me: Gear is a thing. I can't say for pvp, but gear can make or break a character. Gotta gear up. I get bored of Warcraft because of two things: Not action based, and engame is a gear grind. Questing: When a city gets attacked, you expect just that area to be under attack. Here, everywhere is being attacked all the time (quest zones). I understand the reasoning behind this, but it would be nice to see the area at peace when you and your comrads save the day. Warcraft uses phasing to do this. Great mechanic. Very immersive. The programmers here probably can't use their system for that. Maybe they don't know how. Maybe they don't want to. Whatever the case, it is a con in my book.  The faction headquarters can be confusing for new players. If I remember, I wandered around a while before finally getting oriented...
Honestly, I reccommend this game to anyone who doesn't mind (or enjoy's) gear grinding, and to those who feel a city in constant chaos is the perfect way to relieve stress. Personally, I couldn't get past it, but I still enjoyed the game while I did play.

One of the greatest squad based tactics game ever made. A sheer classic to a wonderful series, this game provides everything needed for Strategy junkies to keep you playing for hours.
It mixes Micro & Management well in a world where Diplomacy is also key to surviving the Alien threat. Need more funding? Ally yourself with the political parties. Need more Medkits? Ally yourself with the local medical organisation. Need more scientists? Ally yourself with the local biomedical organisations.
The combat feels alot more personal in this game, you fight the UFO's over a city Geoscape rather than a planet wide attack, the UFO attacks have potential to affect every organisation in the game and can indirectly affect their influence towards you. If one of your stray rockets unintentionally hits a criminal organisations building, they will become hostile and may plan on raiding your HQ if you don't smooth things over.
The game also introduces Real Time combat into the tactical based missions. So if anyone isn't a particular fan of turn based games the game allows you the option to experience in Real Time.
The game allows you to set your own pace, unlike the more recent Enemy Unknown/Within, you don't feel as rushed playing Apocalypse, allowing you to enjoy the journey of the game to it's fullest.
This game certainly stands the test of time as being a great tactical squad based game.

TL;DR, If you dig retro games, you need to play Project Mercury. For more details, keep reading!
Visuals: I love the simplicity of the background. I love the NES and Atari games I grew up on, and this definitely fits that style. Sound: Filled with driving, chiptune beats, it keeps you focused and creates a really great sense of immersion. Story: I love story driven games, and Project Mercury has a good one. A team of commandos were dispatched to eliminate a threat, but something happened. You have to investigate. I really dont want to say any more, I dont want to spoil anything.
This game is so well done. With the retro style of visuals and music, on top of the great controls and enemies, its a great time and VERY addicting. So many times I said "Ok, ONE more time. I got this." I couldnt put it down. The story was extremely satisfying to boot.

Project Mercury is a contra clone with a weird graphics style.  It kind of reminds me of those old vector arcade games, the soundtrack is good, and keeps you pumped up for the onscreen action.
Controls are simple, one button shoots, one jumps, you can hold RB to stand in place and shoot while LB changes weapons.  The controls are responsive but the jump takes a bit of getting used to.  When you jump you will move forward as long as you are holding forward, if you stop pressing forward your character immediately stops any forward motion.  This took some getting used to because most games have some form of momentum in their jumps and this one does not.  It does work well though, there are lots of tiny platforms to jump on and just having the ability to stop your forward momentum makes these precision jumps easier.
The level layout is fun and has a few variances besides the standard run/gun/jump style.  There are several levels where you you are on a speederbike(ala 3rd stage of comtra 3), a level that has you climbing a wall and fighting baddies as you do(also like the 3rd stage in contra 3), and a level where you are descending on this weird propeller thing (something similar to the descending levels in battletoads).  Each level ends with a boss, most of them are pretty easy if you make it to them with full health but will definitely offer a challenge if you get there already beat up.
There are 8 levels, levels 2-5 are playable in any order and offer upgrades as you finish them which do help a good deal.  You are given 2 extra lives to complete a stage, each stage has one checkpoint, and if you lose all your lives its back to the beginning of each stage.
The game offers a decent challenge, it is hard enough to keep you interested but not too hard that you will be throwing your controller around.  I think the game managed to nail a lot of things, solid control, varied levels, cool music, and a decent challenge make this a solid title for contra fans at a very low price.

With the latest patch I've decided to rewrite my review, as the patch has largely addressed my issues with the game.
So, Bomber Crew is an interesting game. It's a little FTL-like game set in WW2 where you lead the crew of a Lancaster (or more likely, multiple crews of multiple Lancasters) to victory. Maybe.
The game does a fantastic job of pulling off the sheer terror experienced by actual bomber crews under fire. You're flying around in a long metal cigar loaded up with gasoline and bombs. The only thing between you and an explosive end are a handful of .303 machine guns and some thin sheets of metal someone decided to call an airframe. The game is gloriously difficult, but it's fair most of the time. Enemies can easily overwhelm you if you aren't quick to target them, but they appear in manageable groups that you can deal with as long as you keep on top of it. Sometimes you might need to forgo an optional waypoint, or delay a bombing run, but you can do it. Additionally, the latest update has added an ability to slow down time temporarily, so should you become overwhelmed, or have a group of fighters appear just as you're on final approach for a bombing run, you can activate it to regain your composure and sort the situation out. This feature is entirely optional, with bonuses for not using it during a mission and even an option to disable it completely should you prefer.
However, the game does suffer from a few issues still. The UI lacks certain elements that I feel are vital pieces of information, and the inability to load a previous save and retry should you make a mistake due to a lack of information exacerbates the issue. For example, early on your pilot gains the ability to pull off a corkscrew manuever. It's a great way to make it hard for fighters to hit you, but if you pull it off at low altitude you have a risk of slamming into the ground and instantly killing your entire crew. This in itself wouldn't be an issue, but the game doesn't tell you this anywhere. Normally abilities that can't be used due to not enough altitude or any other conditions are greyed out, like the emergency dive, which you can't use at low altitude. The only way to learn this is through trial and error like I did, as the game doesn't have a section in its guide on the different skills. Even further compounding this is that newly recruited crew, while generally starting out at least slightly leveled, will likely have none of the crucial skills required for later game play. The same goes for the bomber. This can still potentially force a restart if you're at a point in the game where those skills are crucial and your money is too low to reequip yourself. Death needs to be made less punishing because death, even early on, is still essentially a forced restart. You can try to forge on, but after losing my bomber to the corkscrewing accident I was shot down or forced to make an emergency landing on the next three missions, costing me even more as I had to refit my crew and was unable to spend anything on the bomber itself.
You'll come away from this game with war stories of your own. My own personal favorite so far comes from the St. Nazaire raid:
Taking off from an airstrip outside London, the crew of the Dumpy Dustbin began making their way to link up with the fireship. Everything was going smoothly until we started our trip across the Channel. From the sun a trio of Jerries dove on my bomber, cannon blazing away. My crew returned fire, sending one of the Hun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s into the drink before he could pull away from us. As they came back around, my bombadier called out! "U-Boats spotted! Dead ahead!" Quickly ordering him to the controls, he opened the bomb bay and armed the first set of bombs. Flak from the doomed submarine opened up on us, but it was too late. Three 250 pound bombs fell on him, destroying his hull before he could dive and escape. Lining up another submarine, my crew repeated the process, sending a second submarine to the bottom of the channel. After taking such heavy losses, the remaining submarines decided discretion was the better part of valor and dove away. While they made their escape, two more flights of fighters began their attach runs. As my gunners  dealt with them, my pilot set course for a set of gun batteries guarding the entrance to the base. They began mercilessly shelling the fireboat, but with only a meager set of AA guns for defense and my gunners blasting their fighter cover out of the sky, they were easy targets even with the new wings of fighters arriving with every destroyed battery. Finally, the last battery fell silent and the fireship slid into the U-Boat pen. I began to set course for home as the boat detonated, destroying the battery in an enormous explosion. As more and more fighters began closing in, eager to avenge their comrades on the ground and gain some measure of victory, I opened the throttle and gunned for Britain. Even with the throttle at full and all four turrets blazing away the Hun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s were relentless. As I passed over the French coast Bf 110 moved in underneath my plane and opened fire with its 20mm cannons and sending shrapnel flying into my gunners. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ didn't get away with it though, as the belly gunner quickly tore him to shreds. However, while distracted dealing with the 110 a pair of Fw 190s made a pass, cannon fire ripping through my wings. Engine three caught fire and while the engineer was trying to put out the flames engine one was blown completely off the plane. As they passed over, the nose gunner took one of them, but I was in bad shape. With only three engines left, nearly a dozen fighters attacking her and fuel running low, the Dumpy Dustbin limped over the channel. Finally, as we passed over the White Cliffs the Germans broke off their attack. However, life wasn't through with this crew yet. As we made for London, the torn and fraid wires of the electrical systems AND the hydraulics gave out at the same time. Barely able to navigate and utterly unable to lower my landing gear, with only fumes left in the tank but just minutes away from the safety of the airbase my battered and bloody crew scrambled to make repairs. My navigator managed to plot our landing approach and the pilot began to line up as the engineer desperately tried to rewire the hydraulics so we wouldn't be forced to make an emergency landing. At the last possible second the hydraulics spark to life and the landing gear comes sliding out just in time to make a safe touchdown. Battered and torn, but still alive, the crew of the Dumpy Dustbin miraculously landed an equally battered and torn bomber without suffering a single loss. (And then they all died next mission from the aforementioned corkscrew. :D)
All said the issues that this game still faces aren't enough for me to keep my old negative review up any more, and the remaining issues will likely be ironed out as time passes. With a solid premise, a dev team actively taking criticism into account and releasing updates, and enjoyable gameplay that'll leave you with plenty of stories, this is definitely a game that you should try.

For those just interested in gameplay:
Bomber Crew is an extremely fun but punishing game. There is a lot of active management, and even the smallest of mistakes can have the biggest of consequences. For example, you control your pilot by telling him where to go, on top of making sure that your gunners are where they need to be AND you need to tag them just so they can begin fire. On top of that you have bomb targets, pictures, the gunners need to reload, special abilities, etc.
You also earn money every mission in order to upgrade your plane and hire new crew members if you were unfortunate enough to lose one.
All around, Bomber Crew is a solid game with adorable, voxel graphics, and reminds me a lot of FTL.

This is the first game of the famous "Witcher" trilogy. Paraphrasing well-known quote, as every good story, it starts with a big fight and then the tension is rising. Geralt, the main hero of the game, wakes up with no memory and just after that has to defend the stronghold of his people from an enemy attack. As a result, he starts his long journey to find the men responsible for the attack, theft and killing one of his friends. During the adventure, he will be involved in convoluted politics of the realm and will be forced to chose sides and make difficult decisions.
The game offers interesting story with a long main quest as well as numerous side quests which enrich the time spent playing. In a crucial moment of the game you have to chose one of two options, which has an impact on the rest of the game. The choices are not easy, one time you have to chose between two women, the other time you have to decide which side you are on: rebels or militant religious order. It remained me of the first game of "Risen" trilogy, where I was also forced to make similiar choice. As in any good RPG, the game contains information on all little details of its world, which can be accessed any time using diary. The system of magic is simple, but the alchemy offers many elixirs, which can be made using herbs as well as body parts of killed monsters. Its identical to the system in the "Two Worlds" games. The game is polish and there are a lot of Slavic mythology-based creatures, like Lady Midday.
The fight mechanics is frustrating, but after hours of playing you can get used to it. Also, the camera motion is not as flexible as in similiar games and the world is not so open in some parts of the game. Graphics may be irritating sometimes, eg. dissapearing grain fields when they were very important part of the story.
Anyway, the game is good and I recommend it to anyone.

At the point of writing this review I've spent about ten hours on The Witcher. While I'm sure it would've been one of my favourite games in 2008 I didn't manage to enjoy it at all in 2017.
I played the game with the mods recommend in the highest ranking guide here (written by Amstroid) and can recommend doing that to update the game to somewhat more modern standards.
So, let's cut to the chase:
PROS
+ Some parts of the graphics are surprisingly well done. Especially the buildings in Vizima looked terrific though all in all it's quite obvious that the game is dated.
+ The story and backstory. I didn't really progress that far but from what I glimpsed this is one of the selling points of the game.
+ The soundtrack. It's not something I'd listen to in my car but I appreciated it in the game.
+ The atmosphere. Especially the environmental sounds a great!
I'm sure there are far more PROS in gameplay aspects I didn't check out.
CONS
- Backtracking/Walking. I spent a lot of time just doing that. It's not so monotonous at night when the monsters come out to play but it was pretty boring at daytime.
- Combat. It's a weird mixture of round-based combat (like in the early FallOut games) and the usual hack-and-slash of RPGs (like in Skyrim) that just didn't work for me. I died quite often because I missed that my health was low in a fight, and it just wasn't fun at all to me. The Witcher's combat is all about strategically choosing weapons, fighting styles etc. but in a way that felt tedious to me.
All in all it just was boring to me, mostly because of the combat and time spent just walking from point of interest to point of interest. I've heard that it gets much more interesting later on and I hate to abandon a game with a good story, especially since I wanted to use it as the introduction to the whole series.
I can't recommend this game in good faith, but, well, it's 85% off quite often so you can get it for a little more than 1€ (or 1$ I guess).

One of the most fun and conceptually interesting RTS games I've ever played. It's an Original War in more than name.
Good mix of RTS and RPG mechanics. Humans are a limited resource, they do not respawn and you do not receive more than you start with. Each character can gain experience in 4 classes and can change between classes at any time in the appropriate building, retaining his experience. Some things (construction, vehicles, turrets) can be automated, removing the need for a human pilot, but computer-controlled entities are slower, shabbier and do a lot less damage than those controlled by a skilled human operator. You must always find a balance between risking irrepleaceable human staff and wasting resources on suboptimal AI control.
As far as vehicles go, you build your own by mixing together a chassis, engine, pilot (can be manual, remote or AI) and weapon. New components are made available by researching them and/or building addons for a vehicle factory, each of which can only accomodate five - and all factions have at least six possible addons that can be mixed and matched. While higher tech components are generally more powerful than lower tech ones, they never render the low tech ones truly obsolete, by virtue of costing more, taking longer to build and being more specialized (e.g. heavier vehicle turrets cannot rotate unlike lighter ones).
The game is in isometric 2D, but the terrain obeys the rules of 3D in a way no later games did - unit vision works as "rays" instead of a radius, trees and rocks obscure vision, units on high ground see and fire further, soldiers can go prone in tall grass to become virtually invisible, etc.
Terrain layout, elevation, trees have a real impact on gameplay. Infantry uses it as cover and to avoid vehicles, vehicles require a tracked chassis to ascend slopes, and the most powerful vehicle in the game is  balanced by being too huge to climb a hill.
The two campaigns are long, varied and challenging. If you go for all bonus objectives on the highest difficulty, there's easily at least 60 hours of gameplay (though I clocked 120 due to leaving the game running in the background a lot). The American campaign is the best one, having a good story and characters.
The sound effects are bland and lack variety. There is only one sound effect for most actions.
The voice acting in the Russian campaign ranges from mediocre to terrible. This is specific to the English version only - the Polish and Czech versions actually have very good voice acting.
The Russian campaign feels drawn out and padded at times, and the Russian part of the story feels disjointed.
There is no campaign for the third faction (Arabs). You get many glimpses of clearly important Arab characters and see echoes of their ventures happening offscreen, but the campaign that was supposed to explore them in detail was never added since the publisher went bankrupt.
There is no skirmish for the same reason as above.

Original War is a game where your soldiers as your most valuable resource. You are reliant upon only a finite number of troops and must manage these to the best of your ability and limit casualties. The game also features a bit of an RPG system where each soldier can develop as a Soldier, Engineer, Mechanic and Scientist where each class has its own strengths and weaknesses.
And these soldiers if they survive are present for the entirity of the campaign and depending on the choices you make, follow you to hell and back.
Overall I think Original War is a very fun and addictive game that never really got the attention it deserved when it was released.

At the point of writing this review I've spent about ten hours on The Witcher. While I'm sure it would've been one of my favourite games in 2008 I didn't manage to enjoy it at all in 2017.
I played the game with the mods recommend in the highest ranking guide here (written by Amstroid) and can recommend doing that to update the game to somewhat more modern standards.
So, let's cut to the chase:
PROS
+ Some parts of the graphics are surprisingly well done. Especially the buildings in Vizima looked terrific though all in all it's quite obvious that the game is dated.
+ The story and backstory. I didn't really progress that far but from what I glimpsed this is one of the selling points of the game.
+ The soundtrack. It's not something I'd listen to in my car but I appreciated it in the game.
+ The atmosphere. Especially the environmental sounds a great!
I'm sure there are far more PROS in gameplay aspects I didn't check out.
CONS
- Backtracking/Walking. I spent a lot of time just doing that. It's not so monotonous at night when the monsters come out to play but it was pretty boring at daytime.
- Combat. It's a weird mixture of round-based combat (like in the early FallOut games) and the usual hack-and-slash of RPGs (like in Skyrim) that just didn't work for me. I died quite often because I missed that my health was low in a fight, and it just wasn't fun at all to me. The Witcher's combat is all about strategically choosing weapons, fighting styles etc. but in a way that felt tedious to me.
All in all it just was boring to me, mostly because of the combat and time spent just walking from point of interest to point of interest. I've heard that it gets much more interesting later on and I hate to abandon a game with a good story, especially since I wanted to use it as the introduction to the whole series.
I can't recommend this game in good faith, but, well, it's 85% off quite often so you can get it for a little more than 1€ (or 1$ I guess).
Still a great game :)

I personally enjoyed the aspect of having strict class skills that can are used to level up, giving a feeling of being an actual thief, barbarian, battlemage, etc. The major flaws with this game is that it may be difficult for a new player to get into Morrowind in 2016, and the game does a poor job of introducing the player to it many, many mechanics. Nonetheless, Morrowind has a vast, vibrant world; intricate leveling and progression, and a enthralling narrative.

After over 10 years in my game collection (until recently on CD), The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind is one of those game that I always can pick up and enjoy. For the modern gamer, it can be a daunting task to enter the island of Vvardenfell. The game relies heavily on oldschool D&D rulesets where not every spell, or even attack, always succeeds. Yes, the combat system is quite cluncy and a bit outdated, but to me that's part of the charm. It give you the feeling of jumping back in time, into an unknown fantasy world from a tabletop RPG, where you can see, live, grow and interact with this little virtual society in so many different ways.
Closing thoughts: I have enjoyed Morrowind for over 10 years, despite it becoming more and more outdated, and will probably enjoy it for the next 10 years to come.

Just the WW2 Lancaster Bomber simulator we needed but didn't know it! Picked it up on a whim, and 3.6 hours and 5 crew deaths later I still want to keep playing but need sleep to be able to function at work... or do I?
Controls take a little getting used to, and it could use some actual keybinds other than "hit space to go into tag mode" (which I admit you will be doing a lot, unless you have a middle mouse button which does the same thing). Granted, this does mean that the entire game can be played with nothing but the mouse, and it does work well enough, but my only bugbear is having to scroll all the way in to be able to reassign crew roles or fix/put out fires/reload turrets (until you get the autoloader for the rear turret, but I've not progressed far enough to see if it becomes available for any of the others). But then you take into account the sheer amount of fun you can have, and the sense of achievement when you manage to pull off your seventh mission in a row without losing a single crew member (and then having to ditch in the next mission because you've only got the one medkit which your engineer just used on your pilot and then got shot up himself, resulting in nobody being able to actually fix anything in time, and the loss of the plane behind enemy lines, with only two of your crew being rescued... and then the revenge run with a bunch of fresh recruits :D).
Would love to see a plane other than the Lancaster become available as DLC (for example the Blenheim), but even with only having the one type of bomber/recon plane available to you, this is just too much fun... If you are looking for something you can play in bursts, with a certain amount of progression (yeah, your crewmembers can die permanantly, but even if the plane is lost, you don't have to rebuy everything you did to it), and you don't mind it being a bit cartoony, then go for it. It's got its downsides (which for me I've mentioned above), but it's got a kind of Cannon Fodder feel to it that's calling me back in for another session...
A solid 8/10 if I were to assign a score. Would be a 9 with some keyboard shortcuts, and a 10 with some additional bombers.

Even with the high difficulty level and the ADHD mindset the game requires you to possess there is something magical about Bomber Crew.  The game that keeps you coming back asking for more.  My multitasking is getting better folks.  Bomber Crew is making me the pro ADHD multitasker I always dreamed of becoming..

tl,dr: bought this at a massive discount, but was so impressed with it that i'd even recommend it at full price.
Rather short (ca. 3 hours for a playthrough, possibly faster), first part of a planned trilogy (but feels complete on its owb).
While a nice (if somewhat short and mostly easy) adventure on its own / gameplay-wise, the story is what makes this a real piece of art. There is so much sub-text and implications about the value of a life, a moral code and a purpose in life, and it still never gets too direct or makes you feel your _personal_ views as a player are "right" or "wrong".
The game is rather linear, you have very little choice of what to do. But the ability to always question your actions (or deliberately NOT doing so) set the moral undertone of what you are doing and give The Fall a feel of freedom of action.
The actual gameplay is rather smooth, but the interface is rather rigid and impractical, but this (and some repetitive dialogue) adds a distinct feel of the player-characters rigid programming.
The graphics are not technically impressive, but the art-design is very fitting, so that the game itself is very visually pleasing.  Background music, ambient sounds and especially the voiceacting are excellent.
SEMI-SPOILER: I have NO IDEA how the developers are going to do the second and third part of the trilogy after witnessing how the story of the first part ended. Either they have spent all their creative potential with this first part, or the rest of the trilogy is going to be vastly differring in its story.

The Fall is a nice, story heavy puzzle game. The atmosphere is very dark and creepy, and the writing is meant to be thought provoking, something I felt that it succeeds at very well.
I'd like to add that the ending is "to be continued" and that they're working on a sequel. However, The Fall is good enough as is so while the ending is a cliffhanger of sorts, the first episode still has a clear end.
Good things about this game I would say is the voice acting, the story and the atmosphere.
Things that are less good are the controls in combat. They're a bit unpolished and can be slightly unresponsive and frustrating at times. Fortunately combat is fairly easy so it's manageable.
The puzzle difficulty is at a reasonable level. I only found myself stuck on one of the puzzles because I misread one of the clues. Also the key to finishing the final battle was a bit obscured.
All in all, if you like dystopic sci-fi with a creepy atmosphere and a well written story and solid voice acting, and can stand somewhat glitchy combat mechanics, then this game is for you. Worth even the full price in my opinion.
If you want gunplay, this game is not for you. It's a puzzler.

Reviews really are not my thing, but for a game like this I simply have too.
This was one of my first RTS games ever played and frankly it has been stuck in my head since I played it as a child, now years later I find it on Steam, play it and god it still holds up today, I admit the game does have its issues, but the good far outweighs the bad, I will list everything, but keep in mind while there is some small facts in this, most of it is opinion.
I'll start with the bad:
- Voice Acting isnt the best, and in times even messes up its audio making a character speak with different voices.
- Graphics are old, I say old, not bad, back then the graphics were nothing special but they got the job done.
- Slow Paced, If you want to learn this game or just see everything it has to offer, or even just steamroll missions, you need to be patient, things take awhile to start up, building bases, some missions forcing you to wait time limits, the game itself showing you its features and unlocking things bit by bit on each mission,
- Game suffers from start up difficulties and is fussy on how it wants to work, even if you have a really powerful computer, Original War will downright refuse you if it isnt set right. but these problems can be fixed with some tweaking with settings depending on the system, I'm sure that most if not all Original War players had to do something to make the game run properly.
- No Skirmish mode with AI, only players, a mod is apparently being worked on but I don't know for sure. Sure, playing with players is more fun and how its meant to be played, but a little practice would be nice so you have a feeling of the difference in pace from the campaign missions.
And as for the good:
- Open ended story/campaign, the campaigns in this game have so much dialog, possible results and effects with decisions, I have fun messing with the game still after all these years just repeating missions to find all the dialog and effects on a mission, you can branch them out on each playthrough and it will save them going from worst to best result, plenty of replayability if you have the patience. remember, the results of one mission can easily effect another, be it good or bad, the mission after, or a mission much later in the game.
- Characters/RPG elements, This game doesnt allow you to spawn more troops, besides from vehicles and buildings, the people what you have is what you get, if someone dies, your not seeing them again. this makes you want to keep each one alive for multiple reasons outside of keeping the base running, characters are far more efficient at most if not all tasks depending on their class, each class can be leveled up granting them slight stat boosts in defense/attack while being more efficient at the role they are in. This causes tension when a battle starts, should you send remote or AI forces at the enemy? having mediocre stats but can be rebuilt, or should you send your valuable characters with better stats, but irreplaceable on death. The stats of a character are important even when building a base, the higher level engineer you have not only chages how fast a building can be made, but also the quality of its defense increases too, two of the same built at different leveled enigineers, the higher level building will have higher natural defense.
- Easy to Control/Responsive, In an RTS being able to command your forces and view the map is critical, while Original War does have hotkeys, you don't need to use them to be effective, you can play this game pretty decently with just the arrow keys, mouse and shift key, sure you might not be as fast as the pros and in multiplayer the experienced likely know how to group everything well with presses, But its nothing to worry about, in my opinion an RTS needs functionality in its hud and controls or it breaks apart. This has it and is easy to use.
- Speed up/Slow down bar, to counter the bad of the game being slow paced or being fed up of just watching your men do a slow walk from point A to point B and repeat, or even just the time it takes to do a certain building, research or vehicle you can speed the entire game up which saves time, you can also slow down the game speed too which is useful for doing those hard decisions in which unit to attack or even just to time the retreat just right for maximum damage to the enemy and minimal damage to your own forces.
The first two good things though are what really seal it though, its one of those things you have to see for yourself so you can understand, its very gripping, provided you don't mind doing a few reloads as you learn from mistakes. I guarantee it will happen.
For the things in middle.
- Soundtrack suits the factions and moments, but sadly they are short and repeat often, I don't mind it but I'm sure some may get annoyed with its frequent looping. I'd say its best music is the Main Menu music.
- While I said the voice acting isnt exactly the best, I do find it amusing in moments, its the type of bad that can make you laugh at times depending on your sense of humour.
- Similar to the soundtrack, sounds effects are also repeated over and over, its always the exact same gun fire sound and explosion for everything, again, this can be annoying if you want variety or don't like things being heard over and over, but to me anyway, they are decent enough to keep you satisfied, you know what the intention for each sound is and it works.
- American campaign cutscenes are nicely drawn in front of you as the protaganist talks to you, I think its a nice effect, the Russian ones are done much differently, while I like them too for the sake of them looking and feeling different for obvious reasons, the American ones are in my opinion better to observe just for the artistic touch.
- In game cutscenes are included too, but while I get some are nesscesary at times for moments in the game and to know what's happening, some of them are utterly pointless and waste your time doing something unnesscary, example, your given orders and told what to do, but instead of game just loading the next part, it decides to wait as you have to sit there and watch characters move out the map which you cant control or influence, and being the slow paced game it is, at times it can take awhile, nothing too big mind you, but it can be an irritancy to me.
Well I think I've ranted enough, but overall this is a really fun game and I do recommend picking it up and giving it a try at least, I believe it needs more respect than what it got, suire its my inner nostalgic child demanding that but seriously, the title is right, its certainly 'Original' in how it plays.

I have purchased Original War three times; first in a bargain bin in 2002, then on
and finally on Steam. Let me tell you why this is one of the finest RTS games ever made. A truly exceptional example of the genre but mainly for reasons that set it apart from most strategy games.
Let's talk about what it does that may not be so different but is instead allows us a comforting familiarity with what we've come to expect from Sci-fi RTS games. As is a staple of the RTS Genre the single player comes with two campaigns, a Russian and American/NATO campaign. There is the cliché'd sci-fi super-rare-new-resource, and of course it's a green crystal.
What sets Original War apart from most RTS games is... Well, quite a lot actually. For one; it's set in a world where time-travel is possible. Russia and America are vying for control of a new-found substance called Siberite (known as Alaskite in the Russian campaign.) Both superpowers decide to use time travelling machines to go back and move all the  green-glowing-good-stuff to their respective territories, so that when the future comes around they'll already be in possession of every valuable deposit of said resource. For the soldiers embarking on this mission; it means a one way trip. Speaking of soldiers...
Throughout the story you'll be given a single protagonist (American's get Macmillan, Russians get 'Gorky') and if they die, it's game over. The rest are cannon fodder. Likeable cannon-fodder. The problem with liking these human meat shields is if these characters die, that's it. They don't come back. Given that each character has stats based on what you had them do most (building vehicles, constructing fortifications, shooting enemies, or researching space-time anomalies) they get better at it through an EXP system. Even if you don't find yourself liking their dialogue (impossible), you sure as hell will miss their efficiency. Certain characters dying affects the story too, sometimes in a grim way (this is true of both campaigns).
This is but a brief overview of the game, there's a lot more off-the-wall design elements you should experience for yourself and for it's price, Original War will not disappoint. It's difficult to find anything to dislike; The RPG elements are unobtrusive, the cheesy dialogue is heart warming and with memorable characters such as Colonel Powell and Lisa Lawson (to name but a few) I cannot reccomend it enough.
