Mixing games - and genres - like This War Of Mine and Dead State generally seems like a good idea. This isn’t always the case, though, as we sadly all know (and have usually experienced ourselves). So, is this altered remake of the originally-crowdfunded game worthy of your time right now or does it need to be in Early Access a while longer? Let’s quickly find out.
You start off by selecting two survivors from a group of six. All of these survivors have their own skills; one of them may be good in building while another one might be better with firearms, et cetera. Once you have chosen two people you will be dropped off in a house and your goal will be to survive for 20 days (by then it’s already 19).
If you ever played This War Of Mine then you will likely already understand how it all works.
For those who haven’t (yet) played that game; the game expects you to expand your hideout by building and upgrading useful furniture. This is done by looting places close by. All the while trying to survive, take care of your survivors and actively defend yourself from humans and zombies alike.
Your survivors have several meters that you have to keep an eye on: sadness, energy, hunger, wellness and injury. You can increase the meters (or, at least, try to let them decrease at a slower rate) by building campfires and kitchens while also making sure they don’t get hurt too much/get sick and by just letting them sleep every now and then.
Besides carefully watching over your group you can also let them craft weapons (which you should absolutely do if you want to make any progress) and other tools that will help you to (easier) survive those 20 days.
Naturally weapons and gear can be equipped to make your characters more powerful but they won’t suddenly turn into superheroes. These are still (virtual) human beings, and even though they can be shot multiple times before they die they are not invincible: once a survivor is dead you will have lost him or her forever (unless you apply a first aid kit in time) and you can then try to recruit a new one. But it will never be the same as they all have unique skills, which I already wrote about a moment ago. Still, it’s better than nothing. At least with another survivor you have a better chance at surviving.
So once you’ve been dropped into your house you can choose where to go to with one or both of your survivors. By opening the map you can choose which way you want to go. It’s recommended to start in the Easy or Normal areas because otherwise you’ll most likely be killed within seconds. Each area is different; there might be an alley with a house where you can loot of items from (but you still have to be beware of enemies!). In other areas you might be able to find survivors that you can recruit while in others you will most likely get shot by untrusting survivors if you’re not too careful. These are the places you can normally get a lot of loot from, however. The risk/reward mechanic works very well in a game like this, especially considering the setting and tone.
There are a lot of places to loot/scavenge but depending on how many survivors you bring with you you might not have enough space in your inventory to grab just about everything. This results in having to make some tough choices along the way; do you bring a first aid kit with you in case someone gets hurt during the next mission (maybe even the same one?) or will you just grab a few pieces of wood instead so that you’re at least able to build or upgrade that next piece of furniture (that might prove to be even more useful (in the long run)). Life
is hard.
While Forsaken Fortress Strategy isn’t a roguelike you do have to be careful that not all of your survivors get wiped out. Otherwise it really is game over. Thankfully you can save in-between missions, in your hideout. But only here! You can’t save during actual missions. So if you have a feeling that things are going well make sure and save once in a while. It might just save your life (no, not literally, of course). It will save a lot of stress and frustration in the end.
Your survivors can also use stealth and it’s recommended to use it as much as possible in order to prevent unplanned battles. You can’t avoid everything, but sometimes it’s clear when you might just lose a battle.
There are multiple gameplay modes, too. You have Survive, which I have discussed in a little more detail just now, Challenge, where you goal is to get out of the city and Endless, which speaks for itself.
One other thing I’d like to mention, though, aside from the actual gameplay is that the controls do take some getting used to, but so far this - for me at least - only applies to the keyboard controls.
The music is moody and it definitely fits the game’s atmosphere, although it’s a little more up-tempo during battles. There doesn’t seem to be any voice acting and the sounds effects are rather basic, but they get the job done I guess.
The visuals are okay and could definitely use a little more detail, especially as far as the animations are concerned. Keep in mind, however, that this still is an Early Access game. While it clearly lacks polish at this very moment, it’s possible that the gameplay is the main focus of attention right now. So it’s likely we’ll see graphical improvements and more polish during the upcoming months.
I can be really short about the length. Since it’s still in Early Access some content is currently still missing: bigger maps and more enemies, for example. Therefore it’s hard to exactly calculate but you can easily get 10-15 hours or more out of it right now. I think, with some luck, that the story can be completed even faster than that, but I don’t see any reason to rush through it. For €10 this is a pretty good deal!
Forsaken Fortress Strategy won’t set the world on fire, but with just a little more polish it is and will be absolutely worth your time and money. If you enjoyed games like Dead State and/or This War Of Mine then there’s nothing to dislike here. The gameplay is solid and while the rest of the game is still in a relatively early state I expect the final product to look and play much better than what is currently being offered.
Pros:
+ Different gameplay mechanics
+ Six survivors with their own unique skills
+ Multiple gameplay modes available
Mixed:
+/- Graphically it doesn’t look terrible, but there are still some bugs and glitches that need to be fixed
Cons:
- Might be a little intimidating if you’re new to the genre
- Lacks polish
- Keyboard controls can be a little awkward
(Ratings aren’t calculated based on a formula, but on my personal feelings)

I'm not an old fan of the game, i've only seen bits of it way back in 1996, when i was in the german military and one of the other guys had a PS1. I recall the real live action intro, and some other things like a couple puzzles, but thats it.
The game: This game has a very strong atmosphere. I jumped in my seat at least twice, and was frozen when i played in darkness and someone turned on the light in the corridor of the house i live in without an audible sound. I was relived when it turned out to be a neighbor, haha. You really need to think about what you do next. Do i kill this Zombie? My ammo is limited, and if i do it, he might come back as a tougher Crimson Head. I could burn him to avoid that, but fuel is scarce. Maybe i just leave him be? But he could break through the door and haunt me again! While other games just beg you to kill kill kill, this one makes you stop and consider. There are plenty of ouzzles, but nothing overly complicated. There is usually some hint nearby. Also the limited inventory forces you to consider every move you make. Even the often despised save system adds to the tense atmosphere.
Sound: The sounds are very clever. There is no music most of the time, but rather reinforcing moments of music, like when a Zombie appears, or something could jump at you suddenly. Once you reached a saving and storage room, there is relaxing but somber music. But the thing i love the most is how realistic all the sounds are. Whether you walk on stone, dirt, wood, carpet on wood, carpet on marble, weapon sounds etc etc etc, everything sounds realistic. Very often you don't see the enemy, but there is a sound....is it s zombie? The voice actors are good, and they fit the mood. Especially Weskers coldness comes through well.
Graphics: The graphics are beautiful. certainly, much of the stuff is still from 2002, and looks kinda low resolution like, but that even adds to the unreal haunted house atmosphere, and just improves immersion. I think a version ith high res textures and such would even ruin some of the atmosphere. You feel like you are in an old B-movie. And just like those movies, the derelic look just adds to the desolate, lonely feel of desperation. I also appreciate very much the fixed camera angles, which often feel like something is watching your character...something terrible under the table, behind the fence, or on the ceiling. The character models however are very detailed. Maybe not state of the art like, but they look very realistic. For example on Jill you can see the elbow, knees, shoulder blades, biceps, collar bones etc. They are not buff stick figures but rather fit and beliveable people. The animations are very different between Chris and Jill. Jill for example has a slight swing in her hips whether she walks, clims ladders or runs, while Chris is stiff as a board. Even when they are attacked by the same insect in a certain room, they move different. Jill is flailng her arms uncontrolled, while Chris tries to wave away the little bugger.
Characters. There are a lot more cutscenes than i expected. With Chris you work mostly with Rebecca Chambers, and with Jill its Barry Burton. But the supporting characters don't just do the same stuff, no, its very different. That makes playthroughs with both characters very rewarding. Their personalities are also distinctivly different. Chris is clearly the big brother to his little sister Rebecca, doing encouraging thumb ups or pat her shoulders, which she appreciates. Jill and Barry are more like equal partners, with Barry being the more experianced one. Fortunatly none of that feminist stuff is there. They are not tough as nail ♥♥♥♥♥es, a trope beaten to death in modern media, but rather believeable. When Jill first sees a Zombie she panicks and Barry busts in to help her ever now and then, but she is also very capable, breaking door locks, or shouting at Wesker. She is not afraid to wrangle with a Zombie either. Jill is a great female character, weak and inexperianced first but becomes stronger over time. Working through her fears, instead to act like she had none. Clearly the makers of the game weren't infected by political correctness.
Detailing: There are tons of details in this game. When the characerts move through the derelict parts of the house, they stir up some dust, whether you run or walk through water puddles there are different sized splashes, the detailed character models, the different sounds, particle effects like weapon fire or dust, Zombies bodies dissappear once a bigger opponent shows up in the Spencer mansion, and so on and on and on. My favorite part of the game is probably the small path to Lisa's shack. The dark wood, the mist, the mansion in the background, its just so dark and beautiful!
Verdict: I never played any version until this HD version, and therefore i can't say whats from the 96, 02, or 15 version, but i always had the feeling it was done by people who love this game and want to make the best version possible, whatever version it was. There is none of the cynism that modern games often have. Can't win against the big boss? Buy this great DLC!
If you have patience, like immersion and atmosphere, and don't care for blazing guns all the time, buy it. Its the first of the original style with fixed backgrounds Resident Evil games i played, and i just can't stop! For people who love to unlock stuff there is some of that as well. Different costumes, weapons, modes and ending movies.
I didn't encouter any bugs, freezes, or crashes, it worked just fine.
Its obvious to me how great the design of this game is, and that this is a classic that even after almost 20 years still is able to sell a million+ copies with just a slight graphics update! Can anyone remember the Call of Duty game two numbers before the current one? Can you tell apart any Assasins Creed game? Whats the difference between the latest FIFA game and the one from 2011? This game has heart and soul, and a brain, too.
Buy it.

Just got past the St. Nazaire Raid i.e. first Critical mission, here's my thoughts so far:
- graphics are simplistic and stylised, but do the job, you can tell what is what and mostly match the upbeat mood of the game
- music tucks you in for a nice Lancaster ride in 1942, audio sounds good, not much to say, there's no voice acting, your recruits and NPCS only make those grunts
- gameplay itself can be described as a simplified B-17 Flying Fortress combined with FTL, you get missions of varied difficulties, most of the time to bomb something and you're there to make sure you do the task without your bomber falling apart, each mission rewards you for success and can trigger events like lowering enemy damage, there is also a chance of a penalty for the course of the mission such as enemy aces skulking about
- it is also ABSOLUTELY HECTIC, as soon as the action starts you're dealing with multiple things happening at the same time, you're moving crewmen around and scanning the sky for target and assigning a nav point to your pilot and opening bomb bays and arming bombs and dispensing crew abilities while half of your engines are on fire and THERE IS NO PAUSE BUTTON
- crew abilities are absolutely vital to success, I'm not sure if I would be able to finish Operation Chariot without my Navigator assigning manual nav points (to avoid enemy hot spots) and my mechanic using the Lean Mixture skill (we lost half of our fuel even before reaching the target)
- I have yet to comment on the overall difficulty as I'm still at the start of the game
- there's a barbie doll element to both your crew and your bomber, you can dress them up or equip with items that raise or lower certain abilities/resistances, your bomber can be customised to be faster, better armoured, equipped with better quality systems and/or better firepower, can't have everything though
- sending your gunners to rearm was initially obnoxious, but I was able to unlock automatic feeders to turrets which kinda nullified that complaint, the only other one I have at the moment is that you need to manually scan the sky for your gunners to engage anything, but maybe there's an item for that as well

I've played this game quite a lot and OMG, I really wish I hadn't.
Firstly, the character creation process is terrible. Everything is where it shouldn't be and you're likely to end up looking very derpy.
The game claims to use "action combat", which is RaiderZ style combat; you have to actually hit the enemy. DCUO does not use any real type of action combat, it's just target your enemy and you'll never miss while button mashing every power. Some enemies are also rather buggy (mainly the HIVE ironically) and don't seem to be taking damage.
As far is gameplay goes, it's just grinding... all the time, non-stop. You gain barely any experience from killing enemies so your only real source of levelling are the awful quests that are generally given to you by your mentor who clearly can't do things themselves. The questing is something akin to that of games made by Perfect World: Kill several monsters; collect their stuff; go gathering stuff; repeat; raid copy-pasted dungeon.
The download for this game is a nightmare, the Steam download is 20gb! Then you also have to start the game and let it re-install on the "Station". I had to leave my laptop on over-night just to download this game.
The game may be free-to-play, but it is definately pay-to-win. Most powers are DLC only and if you want cool stuff, you'll need to use the cash-shop or subcribe and pay monthly. Despite all this, if you were playing with friends as I was, you will probably have a bit more fun.
3/10 Would not play again.

There's something about trucks that work well in physics-based games. Truck Dismount hinted at what was possible in 2006 and ten years later we have Clustertruck, a platformer where navigating to the end of each level is almost secondary to surviving the cavalcade of trucks pelted at you.
It feels like the title was decided first, and a game made around it. That's no criticism of it though. The joy of just seeing the trucks moved, jostled and destroyed in front of you is an experience in itself. The game is made up of a number of themed worlds that introduce more and more elements to keep you on your toes. From simple barriers to jump through to moving lasers to dodge as you progress, the game challenges you gradually, and throws a new problem just as you feel like you've mastered what the game has to offer.
The level design can seem chaotic, but there is often a clear path to follow amongst the carnage. There are few levels where the path to the end is not apparent, particularly the last level, but otherwise it's relatively straightforward.
The platforming and controls are adequate. I played the majority of the game with a controller, and while I found jumping between the trucks easy enough I found turning to be quite difficult with the stick. I also feel you don't have as much manoeuvrability in the air as I feel you should.
Clustertruck is not a very deep game, but the experience of truck-hopping in this sandbox was quite enjoyable and something great to play for 10-15 minutes at a time. Simple platforming goodness.

Ok ok ok, I'm getting ahead of myself. Let me explain why you need to buy this game.
Pros: STORY!!! This is what makes the game stand out. It has an incredibly good story with great, interesting characters. This is what makes it worth playing. Since it's a game and not a movie/comic/whatever YOU are the one making choices, and that is what makes stories in games so immersive.
and for the record: the graphics, music and atmosphere are great and really fitting to the theme. The voice-acting is superb and the dialogue is well-written.
Did I mention that the story is great?
OK, fine. Here are some cons, but they are insignificant next to the amazing story.
Cons: Combat feels a little awkward. It's basically the same combat as Blizzard's Blackthorne from way back in the day. Sure, it feels kinda strategic but it also feels kinda dated to me. And towards the end i felt the cover system bugging.
The UI isn't great. it took me a while to figure out how to interact with things and even then the interaction menu felt awkward.
linear story. You cant alter it, as far as I know. The developers want to convey their story and they're not letting stupid players like us mess with it. (For more information, see minor spoiler below)
Minor bugs and glitches. like the tutorial texts overlapping in the corner. I was unable to exit the options menu after editing key bindings. And melee killing an enemy behind cover several feet away.
MINOR SPOILER: There is a scene where it makes you think you have a choice, for emotional reasons, but you don't. Not as a player. The story demands that you do this, and it does fit your character that you do it, and your character DOES/WOULD make the choice, but it feels more emotional that you have to do it and not just watch a cutscene. So it's most definitely on purpose. I am unsure if this is actually a con or just brilliant writing.
So in conclusion: BUY THIS GAME!!!

I've always wanted to get into the Resident Evil series but have never really had the chance. I was never sure where to start with so many different entries;  so when I saw they  had remastered the original I decided to try it out, It was a great experience. The old gameplay is a little to get used to with the tank controls and claustraphobic camera angles, but after beating the game on the highest difficulty I can honestly say the alternate controls would feel wierd. The combats interesting with only 3 angles to aim middle high or low with a certain random chance of critical strike or headshots.When possible combat is to actually be avoided. It's very risky especially since it only take 2-3 hits to kill your character. Also something I wasn't expecting out of this game but got was a sort of metroidvania feel exploring the spooky mansion or other areas finding keys to unlock new areas to find new guns or parts to other puzzles. Speaking of puzzles they are both intelligent enough to challenge the player yet simple enough to be enjoyable. Throughout the game you will revisit parts of the mansion and discover new secrets. Possibly the most impressive thing in my opinion is how the developers continually up teh ante throughout the game; for example that route you cleared of zombies through the mansion? well now that you've progressed past a certain point in the game a twist happens which fills said route with new terrifying enemies. Truly Resident Evil has stood up to time I had no nostalgia glasses for this game having never played it before, yet enjoyed it imenesely nonetheless.  I can see why people complain about the new resident evils because they do truly pale in comparison from my experience. The sole feature of this game that has not stood up well is the characters/acting. To be honest they feel ridiculous and the voice acting is also very campy, but it has it's own apeal in a B-movie sort of way.

Not familiar with devs history or previous game but this one is heading in the right direction. Ultimately it's a blend of Dead State crossed with This War of Mine on a tighter budget. 3 game modes are provided, Survival, Challenge and Endless. Survival focuses on a 20 day period, Challenge modes goal is fighting out of the city and Endless limits item respawns and such.
Fresh rounds require selection 2 team members, all characters have alternate stats and others can be recruited while traveling to new locations. Employing a map/hub system the game shows all the possible ranges of enemies along with loot that may be discovered. Perhaps in some ways a downside as it leaves little up to chance. Complete missions and return to a central base, where you spend time hoarding loot, upgrading  and receiving some well deserved R&R. Characters can be sent out solo or in teams so while it's possible to scout multiple locations at once, with more rewards comes greater risk.
Decent game of the price and one that surprised me. At the very least it's worth keeping your eye on. More so fans of survival sims/rpgs like those I've mentioned above. Cheers.

Great game hampered by lack of pause button. It's similar to FTL, but even FTL has a pause button for when things get crazy. Well, your 3rd mission in things WILL get crazy.  The graphics, sound, customization of crew/plane are all great. The mechanics of taking care of the plane, focusing fighters, navigation, all great.
But it's that ONE issue, that lack of pause button that just ruin the game for me (and apparently, many others - there's a
).
The devs also explained in that thread that "
"
But it seems pretty silly if that is truly the reason for not including a tactical pause. For one, an actual bomber crew has assigned and understood responsibilities and operate these responsibilities independently of just 1 fellow member (us, the player, who tells all crew members what to do in a sequential manner). A gunner, for example, isn't going to delay their targetting of a fighter because a different crew member needs to repair a radar, or because the bombardier needs to look for the target first, etc. They operate as a team, but also independently of any one other crew member. And by having the player micromanage each action without pause, that is what happens (each event is sequential vs simultaneous).
Secondly, those looking for a "realistic experience" aren't going to be playing a little game like this, they'll be playing more realistic simulators. It's a different demographic altogether.
Anyway, for that one issue (lack of tactical pause) ONLY that one issue,  I cannot recommend this game to those who would expect a Pause button. Of course, some gamers don't mind the lack of a tactical pause, so for that demographic, they will probably thoroughly enjoy the game.
I've stopped playing the game, for now, to avoid going over the 2 hour refund window. I'll keep the game as long as I can in hopes that the devs are willing to address the issue. If not, then it is a wasted gem of a game (for those who place a high value on a tactical Pause).

The Fall is a very hard puzzle solving game with a very interesting story. Without delving too much into the story itself, the characters are interesting and the situations presented are subtle but thought-provoking nonetheless. This is the first of a series of episodes it seems like, so don't expect a long term engagement. In fact, the game seems perfectly suited for its length: not too long, not *too* too short.
Gameplay-wise, the game could use some polish, I think. The controls are fine and respond well, but the way you interface with puzzles could use some streamlining. It's quite easy to walk past major items you need for later in the game, as well. The puzzle designs are quite challening and have a high difficulty curve as well. Some of them are farily straightforward, others require backtracking to almost irrelevant items you came across before. The combat sequences don't seem especially challenging or rewarding and seem to exist more as a check box that "yes this game has combat...sort of."

There's something about trucks that work well in physics-based games. Truck Dismount hinted at what was possible in 2006 and ten years later we have Clustertruck, a platformer where navigating to the end of each level is almost secondary to surviving the cavalcade of trucks pelted at you.
It feels like the title was decided first, and a game made around it. That's no criticism of it though. The joy of just seeing the trucks moved, jostled and destroyed in front of you is an experience in itself. The game is made up of a number of themed worlds that introduce more and more elements to keep you on your toes. From simple barriers to jump through to moving lasers to dodge as you progress, the game challenges you gradually, and throws a new problem just as you feel like you've mastered what the game has to offer.
The level design can seem chaotic, but there is often a clear path to follow amongst the carnage. There are few levels where the path to the end is not apparent, particularly the last level, but otherwise it's relatively straightforward.
The platforming and controls are adequate. I played the majority of the game with a controller, and while I found jumping between the trucks easy enough I found turning to be quite difficult with the stick. I also feel you don't have as much manoeuvrability in the air as I feel you should.
Clustertruck is not a very deep game, but the experience of truck-hopping in this sandbox was quite enjoyable and something great to play for 10-15 minutes at a time. Simple platforming goodness.

I got this during the winter sale on because I vaguely remembered the game, so I got this for 8.99. But, I can safely say this game is worth it. It's an odd mix of chaos, parkour, and speedrunning.
Some levels are panic driven to just get to the end, and others are almost puzzle-like with it's layout. The puzzles are not my favorite, but they're unique and interesting. Note, that there isn't many complicated moves in this game, its only jumping off trucks plus the various abilities (That don't feel overpowered, but fun to use and mostly utility). There will be less moves than other parkours games, and bears more of a resemblence to platformers. The gameplay doesn't get too stale, as abilities add new aspects and strategies, and new mechanics are introduced regulaurly throughout the campaign. There is also a 'ghost' mechanic, that lets you view the path through levels that you, your friends, or the best time globally used while you complete the level.
Overall, I'd recommend this game to anyone who thinks the concept of Clustertruck would be enjoyable as it is well executed.

This was my first experience with the early titles of Resident Evil.  Having grown up with the NES and SNES, I am no stranger to old games. When I first started playing this one though, I thought the aiming and movement was clunky and I didn't understand why everyone loved it so much.  I stepped away from the game and came back the next day to give it another chance, and to my surprise, I began loving every minute of it!!
Let me begin by saying that this game has a steep learning curve.  The first time you play it, you will hate it. But after you start to understand the mechanics, this will quickly become one of your favorite games ever!!  There is a reason it is on most "best games" lists,  So stick with it and you won't be sorry.
This game doesn't hold your hand.  You begin with very limited amounts of ammo, and you should beware that you shouldn't kill everything in sight. You have to search everything, and I mean everything.
I wouldn't say this game is scary the way modern games scare you (with jump scares, greusome depictions of death, and other nonsense), but what this game gets right is the atmosphere.  I prefer more atmospheric horror titles and I am very pleased with the creepy setting of the old mansion that causes a slight jolt each time the loud thunder catches you off guard while tip-toeing through the seemingly abandoned corridors.
Like most older games, something about it is addictive.  You will continue to come back to this game without knowing what is drawing you in.  Something about searching every inch of the mansion to find small tools that will help you along the way is extremely satisfying. It reminds me a lot of old Nintendo games that just feel good to play without any apparent rhyme or reason behind it.  Get this game.

Puzzles play a main role in this game, with enemies being a constant threat to your survival while you wander through the great Spencer Mansion, probably one of the best game settings ever.
A great soundtrack accompanies the player through the game, further increasing the immersion of the game.
Story-wise this game is nothing new, and it dosen't have to be: We got Chris, Jill, Barry, Rebecca and of course Wesker all in one game, RE fans can't ask for more. The somewhat cheesy voice acting returns as well.
The only two negative points I would like to mention are, firstly, the "new" control scheme. It feels out of place for a RE game, as you have to readjust your thumbstick every time the camera angle switches. So my advice: Stick to tank controls!
Secondly, some backgrounds do look blurry compared to others (Aqua Ring being the best example for this).
Some people also reported slowdown problems during cutscenes and a few other bugs. Can't say much about that, since the game runs butter smooth for me.
One of the best games ever made, Resident Evil HD REMASTER takes the 2002 Gamecube REmake, polishes it and let's us relive the terror of Resident Evil in it's purest form.

This is a game from another time. It follows RPG adventure conventions from 10+ years ago. At the time it came out, it was far ahead of its time. Today, it stands as a paragon of the previous generation of RPG system design. Not everything is perfect - far from it in some cases - but what it attempts, it does extremely well.
Your attacks won't always hit - this is the kind of game that does dice rolls behind the scenes. So one of the most common critiques of Morrowind is that you'll swing your blade a thousand times at an an enemy and only deal damage to them once or twice. The leveling system is also really weird - you gain attribute points based on the skills that you've leveled up. Each skill aligns with a certain attribute, and you can choose to make skills either "major" or "minor" skills. "Major" skills, like in Oblivion, are the ones that will count towards your level ups. Once you level up 10 major skills, you'll get a level and your attribute progression will end. So a lot of min-maxing strategies center around leveling up minor skills to make sure you maximize your attribute bonuses.
Sound confusing? It is, a little bit. I always keep a physical tally of what skills I level up and how close I am to a level-up. You can read more online, like at the r/Morrowind subreddit or elsewhere. It's not super necessary to min-max anyway - Morrowind is actually one of the easiest games to become a total god in.
What are the advantages of Morrowind over later Elder Scrolls games? The world-building, the lore, and the quest structures. You'll feel like a real participant in this world - that's something that Oblivion and Skyrim can't always boast of. I always felt like a super-powered player in those worlds. In Morrowind, you'll be just another pawn on the board. Working your way from pawn to queen is one of the pleasures of the game.

A REALLY fun game with a lot of potential for MANY hours of satisfying play. While the most common, and lazy, comparison will be FTL the game actually has it's own thing going on. I can also see the inspiration from M1 Tank Platoon and B-17 from the past. It's not the first game to try this formula but it may be the first to achieve the balance of fun and depth.
At the moment, it's a lot to balance at first. You need to keep cool in combat. Don't panic. Learn to make fast and efficient decisions. Learn to perform series of tasks such as: Send bomber to station. Open Bay doors. Navigate to target. Select payload. Drop bombs. Then tell pilot to climb to higher altitude to escape Flak. Once out of danger, drop to low so navigator can see. Pick next target or go home.
It's all about learning these moves so they are reflex, not thoughts. Good luck and have fun.
Definitely worth buying if you like management sims and war sims.

Plenty of reason to get this over the cheaper, original Lost Chapters version of the game. Without giving into nostalgia of the former shadow, or disguising bitterness of there being a newer improved option on the market, I'm going to be completely honest and tell you why...
It's like this, Anniversary is basically an enhanced version of Lost Chapters. The textures are redone, yet faithful to the original and the character models have been replaced to support newer types of rendering and shadowing techniques.
+ 4K HDR support
+ Unlocked framerate
+Ultra Wide Support
+Better U.I than the original
+ Mods support for future-proof
- Less visual options (not good for people with integrated gpu's)
- The kids faces lol They look so weord and creepy, why?!
- Could have made an option to play the original version or the new version at will
Technically, the Anniversary edition is far more advanced and future-ready. Less options than the original versiins but there is reason for this. It's far better optimized and the real way Fable was always meant to be played.
This new remastered version of the game actually has better contrast, more colours and the faces have more liveliness than ever before. Also, the shading has been totally redone so the game looks so much better on a 1440p and above.
Unless you have a monitor with say, lower support than 1080p, it would be a shame to buy Lost Chapters over Anniversary at this point. If you have a system which utilizes 1440p and above, this version is really going to shine.
(With an 860m gtx 2gb mobile gpu, I'm getting 120fps with maxed settings in 1080p. What does this tell us? Well, that optimization was a priority  this go around)
Fable Anniversary is the definitive way to play, if you want all the bells and whistles if new technology for an old classic! It's what a true remaster should be, what else would it be? :)

After playing this game in my youth, several times, to finally be able to play it again was truly of pleasure. Never in my 17 years of gaming have I ever found a videogame as signature as the original Fable. The guards, the collectibles, and much of the soundtrack is completely original, especially considering the intitial release date. Even as a matured person, the characters were still meaningful, and I actually cared about them, making the game's final decision that much harder to finally take.
But none of these things compare to the good and evil complexes found in the game, as it is the main theme. Fable stays true to itself, unlike the majority of videogames, as it sets it's sights on the idea of being a Hero, and never lets that theme go, which is something that I truly appreciate. Just as it describes, every action does have a consequence, and should you so desire to be the most evil person in all of Albion, it's achievable, as is the vice versa.
I was tempted to give this game a 10/10, which is my score for the original game, but I know that much of my love for the game was from nostalgia, and upon the realization that for new players, this game might not be as spectacular, I settled on a 9/10.

1978, the year one game shifted arcade video gaming from a novelty to serious past time (or a violence addiction if you believed the media of the time). It was called Space Invaders, and it’s humble developer, Tomohiro Nishikado will be forever remembered, for good or bad, for time infinite.
Steel Invaders will never make an impact like the original that it imitates, but it is a very good invaders remake. Game play is pure and simple shoot and avoid, but control and firing is solely done via the mouse. Though this makes response crisp, it is sometimes too crisp and, if you are playing in windowed mode, you can go off screen and click on another window and give the aliens some time to do some hankie panky (the kinky kind), while you fumble frustratingly to get back to your game screen. And sometimes your quickness will run you into bullets rather than avoid them.
There are obligatory drops like health, shields and the occasional rapid fire guns. Between levels you can exchange points for upgrades to your ship for better guns and armor. If you are felling masochistic, you have a nice amount of levels to die and fry in, 40 to be exact.
Graphics is a nice clean retro 90’s style look to environment, aliens and your ship, but they are a bit chunky and fill the screen like Sumo wrestlers in a Mini. Music is pleasant and fits the game well but can get a bit repetitive. Sound effects are few but also suit the game. Not much choice in the options screen save the simple Full or Windowed screen, Sound and Music volume and a choice of English or Russian. A mouse sensitivity slider would be nice, as I said before, the mouse is too quick in movement.
Other than mouse movement and chunky aliens, the only other detraction is the firing. Sometimes it is responsive and other times you are clicking in frustration just to get the bullets out.
If you love retro, love Space Invaders or love both, Steel Invaders by Steel Studio, is your must have game in your Larva Lamp lit library.

I recently played through The Fall twice and I was pleasantly surprised with just how good this game really is.  Though bought on a super sale, I would have gladly dropped the $9.99 to pick it up.  Reminding me of the glory days of games like Blackthorne and Flashback, The Fall is a sci-fi adventure with slight horror and drama overtones that gleefully mixes point n' click puzzle solving with an intricate story and some shoot 'em up action.  In the game you play as the living robo-suit Arid who is trying to get her pilot/operator to a medical bay after crash landing.  The journey with take you through a derelict robotic depurposing facility where all is not as it seems and the story will throw a few twists at you that are unexpected (I didn't expect them!).
The game is simple enough to pick up and play but with puzzle complexity and slight backtracking that might even stump the seasoned adventure fan.  I'm pretty seasoned as a gamer in general, but even this game caused me to check a walkthrough once (I couldn't figure out that crying baby bit) and it took me 2 playthroughs to get the majority of the achievements (still missing one and no clue how to get it!).  After 2 run throughs though I'm thoroughly satisfied with my time spent and probably won't be running through again, but overall the game is very enjoyable.
So as Arid the organic combat suit you will need to figure out what's exactly going on with the rather lively artificial, highly personable AI at the facility while fetch questing, puzzling and shooting your way into the heart of the maelstrom.  The puzzles were challenging on the first run through and some of the solutions are a bit more obtuse than they had to be, while others actually make sense in the game's unusual world.  You will acquire certain powers/abilities in key situations of the game play where Arid is in danger and utilizing these will get you through some tough spots.  If you haven't played yet I don't want to reveal exactly what these puzzles and situations are, but they were unique and took me back quite a bit in terms of old school games in this particular genre.
The side scrolling action plays well with the controls being mostly responsive, though sometimes you'll need to shoot or do something quickly and it's a pain in the keester to get Arid to turn in the direction you need her to using the key/mouse set-up.  Other than that, shooting, jumping, using items and exploring work out pretty well.  The controls are loose enough that you'll make some mistakes but tight enough that you won't die over and over again.  As a character in itself, the facility is dead yet alive with several unique sections with lots to do.  A few of the puzzles might stump you for a bit, requiring you to re-read some of the game's notes, in turn with trying every single item you have on every single key location.  The tasks and enviroments switch up enough to keep things from getting boring and the slight combat runs with enemy droids provide enough variety for a cool shakedown of elements.  You can take cover while shooting which works well and go for headshots as well as upgrade your gun to automatic.  None of this is problematic unless you need Arid to face a certain direction posthaste.  She's not going to do it, so forget coaxing her!
A huge asset of the game is the sound design.  The desolate washes of atmospheric noise, metallic clanging of the facility itself and the well-spoken dialogue of every character was well-above par for the genre.  You will even feel for a few characters you encounter thanks to their passionate delivery of the material.  The game is not uplifting in the least and it takes you down a rather dark, emotional black hole from which there is no escape.  All of these ideas only further to enhance the story which despite being a single episode of a three part series, it plays off in angular ways to keep your interested for the long haul.
The Steam achievements are cool little in-game secrets that are like their own mysteries and a second playthrough plus plenty of trial n' error helped me to achieve most of them.  Thankfully, once you have the puzzles and shooting segments down pat, you'll probably blast through a second run in an hour.  Ala Shadowrun and other such games there are choices of dialogue to be made when interacting with characters.  Some of which will lead to achievements, though they have no real bearing on the story itself as there is only a singular ending to be found.  For even more variety, there's a pretty fun boss battle contained as well...another surprise for me as I didn't think this only semi-combat based game would leave any room for a major confrontation.  I'm a big fan of the old school set-up with bosses and the like, so this was a cool addition.
Graphically, The Fall looks pretty great for a side-scrolling action adventure and is comparable to the detail in Deadlight.  Intricate backgrounds and bleak, foreboding foregrounds make you want to push further and further while missing dinner  so that you can see what's right around the corner.  It's not the best looking game I've ever seen, but the level of detail given to the enviroments is still impressive in 2015.  Besides, graphics aren't all that's important.  If you don't have gameplay you don't have sh*t, The Fall has enough gameplay to keep you satisfied.  I finished my first playthrough in about 4 hours which from my research now is a bit longer than most, but the puzzles did have me running around and backtracking trying to figure out their solutions.  I'm not a walkthrough guy unless it's an extreme case, so as stated I mostly refrained from peeking at those, doing my best to figure out the solutions on my own and on a first playthrough it took a decent length of time to finish a rather short game.  My second playthrough lasted barely an hour at most, so if you're a whiz kid that can figure out things quickly or resort to frequent tips, you'll mow this things down in no time.
Overall, I really enjoyed my time with The Fall.  It stands right beside Deadlight and Gemini Rue as one of my favorite adventure/action themed side-scrollers of recent years.  There's not as much hacking, slashing and blasting as Deadlight but The Fall doesn't need an overabundance of said element.
Pros:
-Cool visual design and detailed graphics for a side-scroller
-Excellent sound and audio cues
-Eerie atmosphere with a great story
-Superb voice acting
-Old school action/adventure gameplay that moves at a brisk pace
-Puzzles, shooting, character interaction keeps things flowing and interesting
-Awesome main character that makes you root for her plight...like Samus Aran with alot of personality
-A bit of replay value
Cons:
-Some puzzles/achievements are pretty obtuse and tough to obtain
-Could use more replay value
-Rather short
-Most of the controls work fine, but turning to face your enemies and get a shot off is a b*tch!!!
-A couple of tedious, ad nauseam dialogue interactions (not many)
-Though glad more parts are on the way, worried they will all be at full price (but hey I got this one on sale, so...that's cool!)
Really, my nitpicks with The Fall are pretty minor.  For about $2 I got 7 hrs of gameplay that I really, really enjoyed.  In terms of gameplay content, atmosphere, story, sound and graphics, I was more than pleased with this game.  I can't complain too much about what I got and it was alot of fun reminding me of a combo between Metroid, Flashback, Blackthorne, etc.  I'm worried that each sequel will be full price and hope there's a discount for those that own the first, but no matter what, I'll buy 'em and play because this game was killer.  I really hope to see some improvements to the turn/movement/shooting mechanic in the future though. That was an s.o.b. of the highest order and I'm pretty sure it robbed me of a few achievements.
Rating:  8.0/10

==============Pros================
- Pretty simplistic but fun. Swooping around is so relaxing.
- The levels are always familiar yet distinct.
- Graphics are pretty simplistic too but charming. The levels look similar but a different coat of paint in every world makes for some pretty awesome scenery.
- There isn't that much in terms of sound here, crashes, the portal sound as you glide from one world to another and the wind whirling as you build up speed. Normally minimal sound would be a negative but here I think it was intentional. The game is relaxing and its peaceful atmosphere benifits from not much sound. Plus if you play your own music it over (like I do), there won't be any clashes.
==============Cons ================
- I don't have many complaints but I think the scoring is a bit off. Sometimes you can pull off a really tight space or close call and get no points for it. It kind of discourages taking risks when there are no benifits, other than your own satifaction of course!
===========Conclusion================
With a very modest 3 euro price tag, 1.50 on sale right now, this game is a steal. Honestly souring between cliffs while listening to Radiohead or David Bowie's 'Heroes' were some of my most memorable game moments this year. This is the antithesis to the AAA FPS game, this game's fun derives from its peaceful, soothing atmosphere and tight gameplay. As for the games longevity, although there isn't a tonne of variety here, I can see myself returning when I when to passively do something while I listen to a new album or when I just want to chill.

First of all, I love Resident Evil 1 and 2. This Remastered version is wonderful, but after at least 30 hours using the necessary third-party workarounds like REHDHook (which were not measured by Steam) until the game crashes, I know that I will never be able to enjoy this game at this point. This is the first game for which I have placed a negative review. I don't like being negative, and I have always been supportive until the game is fixed. But this game is different.
This is a great game that's only disappointing because of a performance bug. For more specific information on the 'slo-mo' bug itself, go to the Forum Bug Reporting Thread. Users have literally generated over 95 pages for you to read. It is essentially entirely composed of bug reports and dissatisfaction. My advice: don't have faith in your computer's processing power as you know it. A super-powerful CPU will not make a difference. There are detailed explanations scattered throughout the thread. Place your faith in those, unless you have taken CS or IT courses in college like I have, and know that you will not encounter such problems.
I was one of the people who Pre-ordered the game almost a year ago. It was so cool. There was the slo-mo bug, but I decided to tolerate it until it is fixed. I tolerated it, but it is still unfixed. Basically ignored and/or, according to very recent reports of Capcom locking or deleting threads pertaining to this particular game, censoring reports that could bring attention to this unresolved issue.
I write this review because I no longer desire this game. I will not re-download it even if they fix it. I am no longer interested. I thought that I could put up with this problem forever, if that's how long it took to fix. But no, the slo-mo, the crashing, the lack of any activity by developers, my interest in this game has completely decomposed and no longer exists, and I cannot honestly say it was worth the money in the end.
Sure, try it. Try it if you think you can live with its problems like I did. I hope you find the game worth your money. If you aren't afraid of being wrong and getting ripped off, what have you really got to lose? It's a great remake, but I don't think it will be worth your money.

Footage of game Overview and 2 missions:
Bomber Crew is an active management game. You are spinning a lot of plates here. You have to tell your pilot what to do and where to fly, have crew members make repairs and put out fires, tag targets for your gunners, bomb targets or take pictures, have gunners reload their guns, have injured crew heal themselves, and crew have special abilities to use. Sometimes all of the above happens at the same time; making the game incredibly frantic.
When you aren't running missions: you're hiring to replace fallen crew, buying equipment, training crew, outfitting and painting your plane, and deciding the next mission.
The missions are straight forward; Lift off and go to the objective, do the objective, fly back and land home. The objectives range from bombing bases or submarines, escorting and defending locations or ships, taking pictures of subs or bases, and a other challenges. The enemy won't take things laying down of course and they will send planes to shoot you down. Sometimes even an ACE will show up and those guys will bring the pain.
The visuals and sound are great, the music really helps amp up your adrenaline as you're managing your crew in the heat of battle.
This game is very fun and I recommend it.

(THE INTRO)
This is my 4th attempt to actually finish this review in a single sitting, their is a LOT to say about the game from my experience with it (over 500 hours according to Steam) both good and bad. I'll get my back story out of the way first.
I picked up the game on launch as another failed attempt to shake loose from WoW, but you know how that song and dance goes... "I can't get my guild to budge on moving away from the game so I have no one to play with" so I eventually had to give it up and drag my feet back to Warcraft with my head hung low. BUT... in the time I did play it, I played the ♥♥♥♥ out of it! It was a new and exciting take on the MMO formula. Using your right and left mouse buttons to execute weapon attacks the way you would in an arcade style beat-em-up, complete with stylish combos and amazing super powers... I was hooked!
(THE STORY)
This is where the game falls a bit flat, only because it involves time travel and I believe that is a very cheap method of problem solving that writers use when they have painted themselves into a corner... On launch the story was that in the near future Lex Luthor finally defeats Superman in a fight (its a kick♥♥♥♥♥cinematic by the way) but fails to see that the heroes and villains fighting each other was the break that Brainiac was looking for to make his move on earth and digitize all data in the universe. So Lex survives and later steals the digitized powers from future Brainiac, he then comes back in time to before Brainiacs arrival and unleashes the powers on the earth giving random powers to the people so they can fight off the coming invasion. Thats about the jist of it... As you might imagine their are also the individual story lines of every big name (and also lesser known) hero and their villians from across the DC franchise...
(THE GAMEPLAY)
As I said above, its essentially an arcade fighter in MMO form. You have access to several power and skill trees that allow you to mold your character any which way you want. You can also change your characters costume/skin/eye/hair colors at any time, even being able to change your gear to match any style of armor you have previusly collected to truely make your character unique.
(THE CONCLUSION)
I like it... Even if you aren't playing with friends your inner child will get a kick out of the sights and combat mechanics. Not to mention that the game is largely voice acted, which is almost required in this day and age of gaming.

Have you ever wanted to face off against mutant slugs, psycho robots and deadly fish with teeth like razors? Then this might be the game for you
Step into the role of ARID, an AI controlled combat suit who will do anything to save her pilot from impending doom whilst traversing the hellscape of an abandoned robotics factory. She finds friends and foe upon her journey to salvation, a journey that will make her question every rule governing her existence as a machine.
ARID is a pretty awesome character, she grows throughout the whole game from being so subservient in the beginning to questioning her reality and how she has to break the rules to save her pilot. For a machine she is very complex and I felt compelled to see how this story ends. The few other characters you meet are very interesting in their own right; I get a real feeling that each has their own story that would be equally interesting to see how they got to where they are today.
The world in which the game is set, although not large by any stretch of the imagination, is full of things that are interesting and show depth not explored in the game. Finding a few notes here and there giving you details but not the whole picture as to what happened in this place and how it became so decayed and forgotten. It had a decrepit beauty to it that I enjoyed to no end. The story appears simple from the outside but is, I suspect, a metaphor for something much deeper. I had a great time from start to end.
The game plays well for a platformer, the gun controls are clunky and the menu selections aren’t the best. But neither hampers the enjoyment and both add to the charm of this indie gem. The game is full of puzzles and challenges, none of which were too difficult to overcome and gave a great sense of accomplishment when you figured out how to beat them. The sound is great too, the voices are fantastic and really add to the characters, the music is ominous and foreboding and the ambient noises brought some life to the dead world.
I thoroughly enjoyed this game from start to finish, so much so that I have played it through twice now and still had a blast. If this is on sale it is a must buy, at full price you would still get a lot of enjoyment out of it but with the short length you might want to wait. So everyone out there help ARID out and play this game.

The Fall is an independent attempt to create a story-driven science fiction adventure game, and Over The Moon have efficiently delivered the atmosphere, the gameplay and the story.
There's really not much to talk about The Fall, however with the outstanding voiceacting and well-developed level design, it delivers what it promises - which is a story evolving around a suit called A.R.I.D. and it's urgency to get its pilot to a proper medical bay. While the game is relatively short, it's deliberate length actually adds to the atmosphere. And believe me, you'll find yourself wanting more at the very end.
Controls can be a bit of a problem time to time, exactly when you are to make a quick decision. This, actually, costed me a few achievements, unfortunately, but that is fine. I'm guessing The Fall is designed to be played with a controller, which I do not have since I pretty much would like to play anything with keyboard & mouse. - Anyway, there's nothing extra ordinary about the graphics. The dark atmosphere and the artstyle goes hand-in-hand and the overall graphics do add to the gameplay. Also, worth to note, I haven't had any performance related problems while playing The Fall on GNU/Linux. - which I am thankful for. It means a lot to see such titles on GNU/Linux and I apperciated every minute I've spent with The Fall on my Arch.
Voiceacting and Soundtrack are well done, there's nothing to add here. Sound Design is exactly how it should be and the Voiceactors gave their best for this title and they've succeed with an outstanding performance. - Very well done.
Does it worth its initial price? That might be debatable. But does it worth spending time with? Definitely. The Fall is one of those unique experiences for people who would like to explore different approaches to the genre. Again, it does what it promises and that's the exact reason why people who are interested in such games should give The Fall a try. - I promise, you won't regret it.
I'm looking forward for the new titles from Over The Moon, and of course the continuation of The Fall.

I bought this game back in 2007 when it first launched and played it completely through. Never bothered to play again and I forgot most of the story, so I re-purchased the trilogy during a Steam sale event. Looking back on it the graphics were great for the time and the story telling was phenominal (although the acting during some sequences are a bit off) and left quite an impression.
The story plays heavily into politics and making decisions on what you think is right or wrong, and sometimes these decisions have consequences that you may or may not regret later on. You choose multiple paths to take base on decisions you make and will ultimately affect how the game progresses and how it ends. These decisions will also affect gameplay with the other 2 games which is why I'm starting over rather than diving into W3.
All of the combat is point and click, and between each click you are timed to your next combo. Combos help defeat enemies quickly. Combos are achieved through different fighting styles: strong, quick or group. Each enemy is weaker to certain fighting styles, so it's helpful to switch between each style to win. Combat feels clunky and Geralts movements aren't seamless or fluid.
For alchemy, you have to research herbs and things to collect by having Geralt read books. It's worth spending the extra time examining everything around you such as bookcases to help expand your knowledge. I'm not really a gamer who explores every nook and cranny for odds and ends, but it seems necessary if you're playing a higher difficulty. Alchemy comes in handy on a normal playthrough, but if you're playing on the hardest difficulty alchemy is necessary so be prepared to search high and low for ways to acquire ingredients.
In summary: The game has aged quite a bit since it's first launch, but don't let that deter you out of a purchase. If you're into storytelling in a setting with magic and monsters then I highly recommend this game. Don't look too deeply into the visuals, just allow yourself to become immersed in the story and let that be your journey.

It took 6 ♥♥♥♥ing years, but I finally got around to playing this.
The main problem that kept me from playing this was the gameplay, which consists of very basic combat, numerous MMO-like quests, and alot of running around maps retreading the same ground over and over. The first two times I tried to play this game, I just got too bored to continue. This time, I pushed my way through until, eventually, the game's storyline managed to get interesting enough to keep me invested. But... I nearly said "♥♥♥♥ this, I'm done" several times up until I got about halfway through Chapter 2.
Even after things got better, the story is your typical dark fantasy fare: everyone's an♥♥♥♥♥ political intrigue abounds, there are no "good" or "easy" choices to make, and your character will shag anything that moves. I wasn't a fan of that last part, since it combined with a super-strong character that made everything reek of being a juvenile power fantasy. Buuut... I knew that when I started playing this, so it didn't bother me as much as it might have. I knew what I was getting into. Still didn't make me roll my eyes less.
It is very difficult for me to recommend this game because while the story is decent and improves with time, the gameplay is nearly insufferable. I went through this game because I planned to go through all of the Witcher games, and I'd prefer to not just jump in the middle lacking context. Having now finished The Witcher 2, I can say that there are enough references to events in this game to make it at least worth reading some thorough plot summaries. Being able to import your save is always a cool thing too. Sadly this game remains a hard sell despite that.
Ultimately, as a stand-alone experience, I would say to give this game a pass... or get it in a super-cheap sale. Since this game is pretty old, you ought to be able to buy this for a very cheap price, and therefore feel less disappointed if you decide to play it and decide that you can't stomach the gameplay.
As the first of a series of games... flaws that exist here get major improvements in the following games. Is it enough to change my mind on this game? Ehh... a little, but not enough to make me give this game a "yes". But if you are interested in the series as a whole, this game can get cheap enough in sales that if you end up disappointed it won't feel like a huge loss. Besides, you might end up liking this first game despite all of its glaring flaws.

I can't say I recommend this game. I only made it most of the way through the second chapter before I had to stop (and so, keep in mind I didn't actually get that far, I believe there were 8 chapters). I had not played the 2nd or 3rd game at this time.
Overall the game isn't that bad. I like the storyline and concept a lot, I enjoyed exploring the different areas, there were a decent number of side quests, and the characters are fun. Combat is pretty simple and easy to get used to, and there were various learnable skills that allowed for different play types.
However, I had some complaints in the game's design. Many of the side quests require you to kill monsters and bring back parts of the monsters as proof. However these items you cannot get until you read a book about that monster. Which makes sense, but is overall just annoying. Books cost as much as the payment they are giving you, so in the end there is little profit. Then you also need to buy books on herbs so you can collect them. All of my money ended up spent on books.
Once you have herbs you can use them to make potions, except you only start with the basic potion recipes. You're supposed to experiment to find out more. I did manage to make a new potion, but then it didn't save the recipe. Meaning I'd have to remember every single potion recipe, making that ultimately useless to me. You also need certain drinks in order to make potions, of which you only get a few outside of buying them in shops. Which I didn't have money for after buying all those books. You could buy potion recipes, but they are purposefully expensive so that you'll experiment.
My other big complaint was the fact that I'm the type that wants to finish all the side quests, and unfortunately most of the quests had you running to the other end of the map, only to run all the way back to the person, to not find them there. There were quest markers, but they only pointed you to the normal location that person is at, which is unhelpful when they leave. One particular quest-giver I could not find at all, only to realize he was at the location he had originally sent me to in the first place. But not till I had spent half an hour searching for him. The quests in general mean a lot of running back and forth. Some kind of fast travel would have made the game incredibly more enjoyable.
Honestly, the problems I had with the game were overall not that bad, and to an extent what I expected. But they just made the game very boring and not enjoyable to me, despite the fact that I really loved the storyline and characters. The points in which I was actually playing important parts of the storyline was very enjoyable, but the rest of the game felt like endless filler and, at least for me, was not worth going through just for the story.
So I can't recommend this game, at least to someone like me. If you think you'll be fine with these things then by all means buy it, its a good game. I'm the kind of person who reads the negative reviews rather than the positive cause they'll actually tell you what you may not like. Hopefully this will help out anyone who is on the fence about this game.

I love the story and character interactions. I had planned to rush through the main story, but there are just so many details to this world that I just can't resist. Most side quests aren't completely pointless and actually add to the main story, and can greatly impact your experience later in game. A completionist approach is actually the best way to play. There are a few genuine twists in the main plot and the side quests, and many moments where I doubted my decisions. It's like a tabletop RPG, except with much more freedom to explore. I had tried Deus Ex in the past and found dialogue to be the worst part of that game, but talking to people is actually a highlight of the Witcher. Characters will tell you useful things, and I appreciate all the situational dialogue. The "drunk" mechanic is pretty neat but annoying early on. Also, most of the in-game books written by humans are hilarious.
Having said all that, this game does have some problems. The graphics and animations didn't age well (though this means the game doesn't really strain the Geforce 940MX in my laptop), and combat is basically just quick time clicking. The weapons are dissappointing; I found everything that's not a sword to be useless. Chapter 1 is super boring and ends with a boss encounter that's just stupid. Also, remember to save often. The autosaves are few and far in between, and early on I died in a few places where I didn't expect. This is probably less of a problem if you just follow quest lines, but I like exploring on my own.
This is a must have from any Steam Sale, and offers a lot of content even for the full price.

I still have the boxset from this game in my closet since 2002ish. This game is pure awesome. Don't let its retro looks fool you.
Its something along the vibes of jagged alliance. you get character progression and permadeath. Most of the main characters have their own lines and personalities written for throughout the entire campaign; i always tried to keep em alive just for that ;D
other than that, the storyline, while slightly convoluted, simply serves as a backdrop for a great rts/rpg game where you manage not only your resources, but your human resources as well. 4 Character classes where your characters can switch between and gain experience in during missions carry out specific tasks, where soldiers fight, scientists do research and heal people up, engineers start buildings and collect resources, and mechanics drive and build vehicles.
Decisions you make within each mission affect subsequent missions. Somewhere down the line you will be forced to make one which will split your campagin progress into two trees. *spoiler :D*
I really loved the vehicle design in this game, where you slowly overtime research and unlock modules to provide more options for modular vehicle construction. Gun+Chassis+Power source+ wheels/tracks is awesome. I like the really distinctive look of the double gun cars. <3
all in all, this game is worth my 20 bucks then, and the 5 bucks now. buy it. you wont be disappointed.

Original War is certainly a product if its time. It was very quietly developed in the waning days of RTS popularity and developers were first trying to do something a little different. It is the quinessential "Gem" for any fans of the genre. The art style is unique and clever, fantastic music and the concept was innovative. You don't train new men in the traditional sense; you have a finite amount of men, and you can build vehicles part by part (chassis, turret, fuel source) and train local fauna (aka cavemen) to join your cause. Each of your men (and women) have a name, and stats, and a specialty. You can change their roles as a match goes on (sniper, infantry, medic etc...) to suit your needs. In campaign mode, survivors of each battle with gain XP and "lvl up". Having an RTS with RPG elements back in 2001 was something special, but I'm not sure this game is for everyone TODAY. I think if you're a die-hard fan of the RTS genre, this is a great pick! Even if you're a fan of retro PC gaming in general, go for it. If you're looking for a Starcraft killer, move right along.

Don't get fooled by the playtime I have in steam.
This is easily one of the best and most innovative RTS games out there.

There is an editor with the ability to script (Pascal-like language) coming with the game and an alive community over at
.
The campaign offers for 10-30 hours of time, depending on skill and difficulty setting and offers quite an interesting storyline with not too monotone objectives.
Apart from that, there is the multiplayer which may not have too many players in it, but it is still functioning and offers around 15 maps with different gamemodes ranging for regular 1v1 build base battle each other to 2v2 with a twist of disappearing and respawning units  up to 3v3 rampage and 4v4/2v2v2v2 battles. I personally enjoy the way the game handles base building and unit management a lot.
The catch with this RTS is that you can't train units. You need 5 soldiers to attack the enemy? You can't train them like that. You start with a certain amount of people and those you have to stick with. You can't just say "5 soldiers plz" and your barracks will poop out 5 people. That doesn't work here.
Some maps/campaign missions have some sort of unit spawn, but in MP it can be selected and in SP it's doesn't make you OP.
You can train apes or make Computer or remote controlled vehicles to prevent loss of actual soldiers, which adds a really nice touch to the game and is a nice alternative to regular RTS games.
I think everyone should give this game a try, it's one of my most favorite RTS games ever and I can only urge you to consider buying it, especially at such a low price.

The Fall is one of those games that just feels a little special. It's odd how much I liked it, considering how frustrated I initially was with the stiff controls and not-so-well-communicated puzzles.
I suppose you could say that the experience is carried almost entirely by its characters and concept, given the aformentioned stumbling points. It certainly isn't carried by the combat, and there isn't enough substance to the level design to create much of an environmental atmosphere, there's just a certain FEEL to the whole affair, and it truly stuck with me.
It's a rather short game, to be perfectly honest. I beat it in four hours, and I'm pretty sure one of those was spent wandering around like a jackass.
The controls are, again, stiff, but somewhat intuitive (you don't really need to move your hand around on the keyboard), and what combat there is can be approached in a couple of different ways. Puzzle-solving is more-or-less a "try everything, with everything, on everything" affair, though there were some rather clever moments throughout. Voice-acting and characters are absolutely fantastic, and the basic concept is twisted around in some pretty effective ways (not to mention the terrible, terrible things you can do to complete your objective). The presentation wasn't quite what I'd call spot-on, but I honestly think that's  just because I personally would have handled it a bit differently.
All-told, The Fall holds a strange, special place in my heart, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for something a little different.

I'm on the fence with the review for this one. I enjoyed the game, and looked forward to finding the time to play. This game seemed to have lots of things I liked in its trailer, so I bought it when it went on sale. I love Metroidvania-style games, stories about AI, and logic puzzles. The logic puzzles are sometimes a bit unrewarding, but generally this game does well. The story is solid, voice acting is good, and the setting is downright chilling.
Let me focus on the things I didn't like, though. This is a very nit-picky list for a positive review.
The combat was simplistic and easy, especially with the active camo. The game could have been less forgiving with your health, forcing you to sneak around and steal fuel cells from other robots. But then, maybe I would have liked the game less because...
...the controls are needlessly awkward. They're functional, certainly, but I feel like assigning two more buttons to the keyboard would have cut probably half an hour from my playtime. Okay, maybe that's an exaggeration, but still.
In the end, the game is "to be continued" which is another downer. The story arc is complete, but many of your suit options aren't even used. I know I'll play The Fall 2, but I'll wait until it's on sale, as I'd advise those interested in this game.

At first look, The Fall looks like a 2.5D platformer in the Metroidvania vein. It's really not. For the most part, it's an inventory-based adventure game with occasional shooting sections and a brief boss fight at the end.
It took me about four hours to complete the game with occasional assistance from a walkthrough. And I definitely recommend that you don't shy away from using a walkthrough when you get stuck. While I mostly found the inventory puzzles to make sense, some solutions require excessive trial and error.
I'm also not sure the shooting sections fit in well with the rest of the game. In most cases, they seemed like unnecessary deviations from the game's typical adventure-style gameplay, but at least I never found them frustrating. (To be fair, I also felt the same way about the shooting sections in Gemini Rue).
Overall I enjoyed The Fall. It presents an intriguing story and provides a dark alien environment that's fun to explore. If you like sci-fi based adventure games like Gemini Rue or Morningstar: Descent to Deadrock, The Fall is easy to recommend. Gamers on the fence my want to wait for a sale.

Got it for $2 so I figured I'd give it a shot. Tons of reviews said how awesome the story and overall game was so I was trusting of that.
Up-front summary: If I would have paid more than $2 for this then I would have been quite disappointed.
Pro's:
-Dark environment was kinda cool and different.
-Mystery and story AT FIRST kept me intrigued.
-Compassion of ARID made you begin to like her character.
-Hiding behind cover was cool for gun fights but became ultimately useless very quickly when you get to cloak yourself anywhere at any time.
Cons:
-Super annoying control interface for interacting with things. Maybe on a game pad this would be slightly better? I was on keyboard and mouse.
-The lame tests you had to get past just to get to the "meat" of the story were dumb. Most were very straight forward, and a couple were so freaking weird or abstract it didn't make any logical sense at all. But you only have a few items in your inventory so you tend to just click on each option for anything that you can interact with.
-Boss was super easy and straight forward to figure out. Anyone who has played a few games can get it in their first pass.
-Messages on the walls and such were overall completely pointless and didnt do much for the story in my opinion. A couple gave some obvious hints, so once again... useless.
-No real need to play through more than once. I am uninstalling as soon as I finish this.
Conclusion: There are tons of other games better spent "wasting" time on that would be MORE entertaining and would have a better story with better gameplay.

This game can devour some of your time before you figure it out. It's not like a lot of the other match-three games out there, and not just because of the different goal, but because you must learn to choose your moves and date gifts wisely to maximize your scores. This game is hard enough on its easiest level, but when you go to the hard difficulty, and then alpha mode, this game goes to ridiculously hard levels that get infinitely harder one after the other.
While this game features the geeky, the audacious, the mature, the schoolgirl and a few more dates, you will dismiss reality and bribe them with ridiculously expensive gifts just to get them to change their hair. Does that make them paid company? Who cares! You will continue to irritate them all with questions, and they will continue to ask you about their answers like it's a high school exam. You will collect their panties and store them just to give them to a dubious imaginary fairy girl who doesn't tell you what she wants with them.
The girls who are seemingly connected to each other never talk to each other after the intro and thus never find out that you're the town player and dating all of them at once. They will inevitably fall in love with you, even Kyu who is completely aware that you're seducing her with your puzzle solving skills, and then initiate the bedroom activity after your 4th date. You can even do this without talking to them at all! (And yes, that's an achievement.)
All in all - play the game, have fun with Momo the Nekogirl, Venus the Goddess, Kyu the insane fairy girl who doesn't take no for an answer and the others you will either love or hate, but eventually bang because that's the game. 11/10.
